quest:1116.text: Dream Dust in the Swamp. Krazek of Booty Bay says that learning about Nazz is quite a favor. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to bring 10 specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, for Krazek's snuff pouch. Bring it back and Krazek will give you the information you seek. Krazek tells you that learning about Nazz is a considerable favor, and that you have already come a long way from the Shimmering Flats for it. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to gather something. The choice falls on ten specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, which Krazek would love for a snuff pouch. Once you return with it, the information is yours. Green dragons of the Swamp of Sorrows carry the dream dust. Adolescent whelps and dreaming whelps both have it, and both live in the swamp's south-western corner.

quest:1117.text: Rumors for Kravel. Krazek has found what you came for. After calling in favors, doing plenty of deducing and giving up a rare bottle of elven wine, Krazek wrote a letter about Nazz Steamboil. It is too dangerous for Krazek to use, so you carry it to Kravel Koalbeard, out on the Shimmering Flats, and you are asked not to say where it came from. Krazek tells you what the search cost: some favors were used up, a rare bottle of elven wine was parted with, and a good deal of deducing was done. The result is a letter holding some very interesting bits about Nazz Steamboil. Krazek finds it too dangerous to use, and leaves it to you to do with as you will, as long as nobody learns where it came from. It goes back to Kravel Koalbeard, out on the Shimmering Flats.

quest:1130.text: Melor Sends Word. Jorn Skyseer brings word from Melor Stonehoof to promising hunters in the Barrens. Those who have proved their grit across Kalimdor are called to Hunter's Rise in Thunder Bluff for a harder trial. Across the Barrens, Jorn Skyseer watches the crossings and encampments. He carries word from the elders of Hunter's Rise to hunters and warriors who have shown promise in the surrounding lands. Melor Stonehoof, a revered tauren mentor, has marked out a path for them. At Hunter's Rise in Thunder Bluff, you meet Melor Stonehoof. The elder hunter asks if you have the resolve to venture into distant, perilous wilderness. His summons opens trials far beyond the safety of Mulgore, where hunters face the continent's fiercest predators.

quest:1131.text: Steelsnap. In Thousand Needles, Melor Stonehoof sends you after a hyena whose pack terrorizes the wildlife. Steelsnap's hunt breaks with the usual reasons tauren take a life. Tauren hunters take life for sustenance, honor, or wisdom from the Earthmother. Melor Stonehoof asks you to hunt Steelsnap for another reason. The hyena is seen as a threat to nature's balance, bringing senseless violence and fear instead of keeping the cycle of life. Steelsnap roams the canyons of northern Thousand Needles, south of the centaur enclave at Camp E'thok. Fierce hyenas follow him, and together they attack the gentler wildlife on the canyon floor. Slaying Steelsnap and bringing back his rib will end his hold over the needles.

quest:1133.text: Journey to Astranaar. Fiora Longears sends Alliance travelers from Theramore north to Astranaar. There, they report to Shindrell Swiftfire in Ashenvale, where the night elves face war and unrest. Alliance travelers arrive in Dustwallow Marsh aboard the ferry from Menethil Harbor, often seeking purpose in northern Kalimdor. At Theramore, Fiora Longears directs capable hands inland toward Astranaar, Ashenvale's main night elven settlement. The route winds beneath ancient, shadowed canopies and leads into a forest strained by war and unrest. Fiora tells travelers not to mention her name in Astranaar because Shindrell Swiftfire does not know her. Fiora's role is to direct fresh Alliance talent where it is needed. Shindrell welcomes able-bodied defenders when they arrive. Ashenvale remains breathtaking, but it is no longer the peaceful sanctuary it once was.

quest:1134.text: Pridewings of Stonetalon. In the Stonetalon Mountains, pridewing venom has become a threat to the uneasy peace. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from Theramore that orc assassins gather the poison for covert raids. Astranaar's Sentinels send scouts south to claim the venom sacs first. The Alliance and Horde have not declared open war across northern Kalimdor, but their peace is fragile. Skirmishes break out beneath the forest canopy, and quiet attacks take the place of full armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar watch for enemy movements, knowing a careless moment could put their sanctuary at risk. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from contacts in Theramore about activity in the crags of Stonetalon. Orcish stalkers are said to gather venom from wild pridewings around Mirkfallon Lake and coat their blades for deadly ambushes against Alliance forces. Shindrell Swiftfire sends champions to kill the beasts and claim their venom sacs before Horde agents can reach them. Shindrell Swiftfire regrets ordering the deaths of native beasts. Night elves revere Kalimdor's wilderness, and the creatures had no part in choosing this war. Yet Astranaar's defenders cannot let an enemy gather poison for lethal attacks, even at the cost of the beasts' lives.

quest:1135.text: Highperch Venom. Fiora Longears in Theramore tasks Alliance adventurers with journeying west to the canyons of Thousand Needles. There, atop the elevated bluffs of Highperch, roost dangerous wyverns prized for their exceptionally potent venom. While resting in the island port of Theramore, travelers may cross paths with Fiora Longears. While orcs commonly capture and domesticate wyverns as aerial mounts, Fiora points out a far more clandestine trade: the creature's lethal venom. Certain buyers across Kalimdor value fresh venom sacs far more than the beasts themselves, prompting Fiora to recruit hunters willing to brave long distances and precarious heights. The quarry nests west of Dustwallow Marsh, within the towering sandstone mesas of Thousand Needles. At a roost known as Highperch, the local wyverns possess an unusually concentrated toxin. Reaching their nests requires navigating hostile Horde territory and scaling treacherous terrain, where hunters must slay wyverns to extract intact venom sacs before hauling the prize back to Theramore.

quest:1137.text: News for Fizzle. Martek the Exiled in the Badlands has news about indurium for Fizzle Brassbolts. You carry Martek's message back to the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Martek reports that indurium stands up to heat remarkably well, and believes it suits Fizzle's pistons. Flakes will not do, though: Fizzle needs real indurium ore, dug out of the depths of Uldaman at the northern edge of the Badlands, which Martek names as the true source of indurium. Martek asks you to pass on regards and repeat all of this to Fizzle Brassbolts.

quest:1140.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Delgren's crusade against the Tower of Althalaxx cultists reaches its sixth chapter. From Maestra's Post, he deciphers orcish writings recovered from the cult's emissaries and learns that Athrikus Narassin hid two trapped Highborne soulgems in satyr strongholds deep in Ashenvale. Champions head to Night Run and Satyrnaar to shatter the vessels, free the tormented spirits, and weaken Athrikus's power. Delgren the Purifier puts his study of Orcish to use after Ilkrud Magthrull, an orcish courier, is cut down. His peers in the Holy Light often scoffed at learning an adversary's tongue, but Delgren's practical insight lets him decipher notes recovered from the cult's emissaries. They reveal that Athrikus Narassin hid two potent soulgems containing ancient Highborne essences far to the northeast, in the defiled groves of Night Run and Satyrnaar.

quest:1142.text: Mortality Wanes. Heralath Fallowbrook lies dying in Razorfen Kraul, with one last plea for the living. He asks that his wife's stolen pendant reach Darnassus, along with word of his death. In Razorfen Kraul, Heralath Fallowbrook lies mortally wounded among the brambles. The stronghold is overrun by savage quilboar and dark magic, far from Alliance territory. With his strength fading, Heralath manages only broken whispers. He says a brave dwarf named Lonebrow was sent ahead to warn Falfindel. Heralath knows he will not leave the Kraul alive. Heralath's last wish is to recover the pendant that marks his marriage to Treshala Fallowbrook. One of the lair's aggressors tore it from him. He asks any traveler who stops beside him to carry it across Kalimdor to Darnassus, so Treshala learns of his death instead of waiting in vain.

quest:1143.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, demonic rites threaten northern Darkshore. Balthule Shadowstrike directs an Alliance assault on Athrikus Narassin, the ancient sorcerer who commands the cult from the tower’s peak. In northern Darkshore, the ruined Tower of Althalaxx shelters demonic summoning. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the tower from nearby and sees that the threat must be faced now. Athrikus Narassin dwells at the summit, an ancient night elf warlock who directs the dark rituals beneath the shattered roof.

quest:1147.text: The Swarm Grows. Moktar Krin at Ironstone Camp says Belgrom wants the silithid pushed back into the depths they crawled out of. Moktar's own half-dead war party cannot do it, so Moktar asks you to take on the silithid at the dig site to the south. After The Swarm Grows (2), Moktar Krin says Belgrom considers the silithid a threat and wants them driven back into whatever depths they came from. Having already killed the dwarves the Explorers' League sent, Moktar now has a war party in no state to fight again, and cannot do it without help. The dig site lies to the south, and Moktar expects no more dwarves there. Searchers, hive drones and invaders are the silithid to be killed, and Moktar's party cannot leave until it is done.

quest:1149.text: Test of Faith. The Test of Faith is a spiritual rite administered by the hermit Dorn Plainstalker high above the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. It challenges Horde adventurers to prove their resolve by stepping off a precarious wooden plank into the open chasm below. Dorn Plainstalker dwells in a secluded vantage overlooking the wind-carved spires of Thousand Needles, pondering the facets that make up a living being: the mind, the body, and the spirit. Rather than relying on simple tribal traditions, Dorn administers his own trials to measure what truly lies within an adventurer. He posits that while conviction can take many forms, the essential quality is simply having the fortitude to believe in something strongly enough to risk one's life on it.

quest:115.text: Shadow Magic. Marshal Marris calls for action against Shadow Magic in Redridge. Blackrock shadowcasters carry demon-tainted midnight orbs that turn dark energies against Lakeshire's defenders. The orbs must be taken from them and destroyed to protect the town's line. Blackrock strength has always rested on brute force, but the clan's raids in the Redridge Mountains now bring a darker threat. Shadowcasters wield dark powers and channel fel and shadow energies through demon-tainted midnight orbs. These artifacts have dealt terrible losses to the local militia, worsening a war already turning against the defenders. Marshal Marris directs Lakeshire's strained defense from the town center, and he knows ordinary steel cannot easily overcome dark relics. If the Blackrock orcs keep their midnight orbs, Redridge's eastern borders may collapse. Marris orders the shadowcasters slain and the orbs seized so the demonic relics can be destroyed, not put to use.

quest:1150.text: Test of Endurance. The Test of Endurance is the second rite in a series of spiritual trials overseen by Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles. Having already proven their courage of spirit, Horde adventurers are tasked with pushing their physical endurance to the limit by infiltrating Roguefeather Den and drawing out the fierce harpy leader, Grenka Bloodscreech. Dorn Plainstalker, dwelling at the Weathered Nook, takes it upon himself to temper young warriors before they venture into the wider, harsher world. Where the initial rite proved that a traveler possessed unshakable faith and steady nerve, this trial tests physical fortitude. In Dorn's philosophy, true readiness requires harmony between spiritual devotion, mental discipline, and the sheer stamina to survive sustained brutality. The chosen arena for this trial is Roguefeather Den, a treacherous cavern tucked within Screeching Canyon west of Freewind Post. Swarming with hostile harpies, the cave poses severe danger to solitary wanderers. To complete the trial, challengers must carve their way deep into the subterranean roost, sabotage the harpies' gathered provisions, and weather the flock's ferocious retaliation until the matriarch Grenka Bloodscreech herself takes the field.

quest:1151.text: Test of Strength. The Test of Strength is the third trial overseen by the tauren mystic Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles. To prove their physical prowess, Horde champions are tasked with hunting down Rok'Alim the Pounder, an ancient, free-roaming rock elemental, and returning with remnants of his shattered form. Long ago, during the reign of the Old Gods, primordial elementals blanketed the surface of the world, serving their dark masters. When those ancient entities were overthrown and sealed beneath the earth, the elemental spirits lost their tether to this realm, largely fading from physical existence unless bound and summoned by modern spellcraft. A few entities, however, were stubborn and potent enough to linger on Azeroth indefinitely without magical anchors. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such relic, wandering the arid canyons of Thousand Needles as a living echo of that primordial age. The local centaur clans gave Rok'Alim his moniker on account of the deafening, earthquake-like crashes produced when his stone fists strike the canyon floor. Anyone foolish or bold enough to stray into his roaming path is hammered into dust. Because Rok'Alim represents raw, unbridled physical mass, Dorn Plainstalker directs initiates to break the beast as a direct measure of their warrior spirit, demanding fragments of the elemental's stony heart as proof of victory.

quest:1152.text: Test of Lore. Following trials of faith, endurance, and strength in Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker directs Horde champions northward to Stonetalon Mountains. There, a wise shaman named Braug Dimspirit waits to administer the Test of Lore. This trial shifts the focus from physical resolve to an understanding of the world's deep history and widespread suffering. In the sheltered refuge of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker pushes initiates through demanding trials meant to test their spiritual conviction, physical endurance, and martial prowess. Yet brute strength and blind faith alone do not make a true champion of the Horde. Dorn recognizes his own boundaries as a teacher and sends those who have proven themselves to Stonetalon Mountains, where an elder shaman can test their intellect and worldliness. The journey takes travelers north across the dry scrub of the Barrens and into the crags of Stonetalon. High in the mountains, near the entrance to Talondeep Path—the cavern cutting through the rock toward Ashenvale—sits the hermitage of Braug Dimspirit. He watches over an embattled frontier where goblin logging ventures despoil the forests and hostile night elves fiercely defend their ancestral borders.

quest:1153.text: A New Ore Sample. Tatternack Steelforge seeks new ore in Thousand Needles to strengthen the Horde’s arms. The blacksmith in Camp Taurajo sends you south to bring back a sample for testing. Tatternack Steelforge works as a blacksmith in Camp Taurajo, under Orgrimmar’s direct scrutiny. He has already supplied weapons made from local centaur armaments, but still wants to prove his craft to Warchief Thrall. Travelers passing through showed him a strange piece of ore taken from a kobold to the south. When they refused to sell it, Tatternack took their refusal as an insult to his craft and the Horde. You leave the flat plains of the southern Barrens for the towering canyon mazes of Thousand Needles. Kobold diggers tunnel through its crags and cliffs. Bring back unrefined chunks taken directly from them, and Tatternack can judge whether the raw mineral can be forged into weapons worthy of Thrall’s war effort.

quest:1154.text: Test of Lore. The Test of Lore is a trial set by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to Talondeep Path, testing a Horde adventurer's mind rather than their physical endurance. To pass, the seeker must venture deep into the haunted barrow dens of Ashenvale, recover an ancient tome of dragon history, and study its contents before being quizzed. After proving their physical endurance and unwavering faith across the salt flats and plateaus of Thousand Needles, candidates under Dorn Plainstalker's series of trials are sent north to Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. Stationed near the mouth of Talondeep Path, Braug dismisses the earlier challenges as simple physical exercises. To truly serve the Horde with distinction, an adventurer requires a sharp and disciplined intellect, prepared to understand ancient histories rather than merely striking down beasts. Braug directs petitioners to venture through Talondeep Path into the forested reaches of southern Ashenvale. There, hidden beneath the canopy south of Splintertree Post, lies the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The subterranean sanctuary is a perilous ruin haunted by fallen night elf druids and the vicious creatures that slaughtered them. Rested upon a stony podium deep in the lower chambers lies the prize: 'Legacy of the Aspects', a rare manuscript detailing the ancient creation and corruption of the great Dragon Aspects.

quest:1159.text: Test of Lore. This leg of the Test of Lore sends Horde adventurers across the Great Sea to the ruins of Lordaeron. Having answered Braug Dimspirit's initial riddle in the Stonetalon Mountains, you are directed to seek a former human scholar among the Forsaken in the Undercity. After proving your mettle and unraveling the history of the Dragon Aspects recorded in the Legacy of the Aspects, Braug Dimspirit admits his own knowledge has limits. Rather than keeping the trial confined to Kalimdor, Braug demonstrates the broad, surprising reach of the Horde's ties by pointing you toward the undead capital beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. In the damp corridors of the Apothecarium dwells Parqual Fintallas. Once an esteemed human chronicler of the northern kingdoms, Parqual's pursuit of knowledge survived the Scourge and his transformation into one of the Forsaken. Confronted by an outsider claiming to have completed the spiritual and physical trials of Thousand Needles, Parqual refuses to believe you are anything more than an opportunistic mercenary until you prove your worth to him directly.

quest:1167.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Delgren sends you north to meet Balthule Shadowstrike before the assault on Athrikus Narassin. The scout has watched the Tower of Althalaxx and can report what has changed there. Delgren the Purifier sends you north to speak with Balthule Shadowstrike, his sentinel partner. You have purified corrupted relics and weakened the cult's hold along Darkshore's border. Before you confront the sorcerer Athrikus, Delgren wants fresh intelligence from Balthule, who has kept watch from the ruins overlooking the tower.

quest:1175.text: A Bump in the Road. Trackmaster Zherin looks after the track at the Mirage Raceway, and the animals out on the Shimmering Flats have grown big enough that their numbers must be kept down before they wander onto it. You are asked to thin out Saltstone Basilisks, Crystalhides and Gazers. A basilisk once collided with a racer belonging to the goblins, the Red Thunder, and in the aftermath Kronkrider took Zherin on to look after the track. Zherin cannot say what the animals out on the Shimmering Flats are eating to get so big, only that their numbers have to be kept down, or one will stray onto the course mid-race. Clearing wreckage is bad enough, and Zherin would rather not pick it out of burnt animal parts as well.

quest:1176.text: Load Lightening. Pozzik, the head goblin engineer out at the Mirage Raceway, needs materials to shave critical ounces off his rocket-car chassis. Rather than relying purely on heavy metal plating, the goblins salvage hollow bones from local desert vultures to build sturdy, ultralight steering and structural rigs. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers is decided by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust is useless if a racer is weighed down by excessive bulk. While gnome teams obsess over intricate gears and brass fittings, the goblin crew led by Pozzik seeks ruthless pragmatic efficiency: stripping out dense iron framing and replacing it with lighter, hollow structural components wherever the frame permits. Rather than shipping expensive, specialized composites out to Thousand Needles, Pozzik turns to the surrounding salt wastes. Salt Flats vultures are plentiful, their skeletons honed by flight to possess hollow, honeycombed cores that provide great tensile strength with almost no mass. By substituting worked vulture bones into the racer's steering rig and minor braces, Pozzik's mechanics aim to keep their machines nimble enough to outmaneuver the gnomes without shaking apart at top speed.

quest:1178.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Pozzik of the goblin racing team is waiting on a prototype fuel regulator that Gazlowe promised a few weeks ago, and it has not come. Gazlowe is usually very prompt, so Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask what happened, since the gnomes are gaining on the team. Pozzik calls the racing team the pride of goblins, and says many people help it in one way or another. Gazlowe hunts down parts from all over the world for the team, and once even came to work on one of their rigs. A few weeks ago Gazlowe said a new prototype fuel regulator would be sent, but nothing has arrived, which is unlike him. With the gnomes gaining, Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask Gazlowe about it.

quest:1179.text: The Brassbolts Brothers. Pilot Longbeard in Ironforge needs a courier to deliver a crate of reinforced siege engine helmets across the sea to Kalimdor. His friends, the Brassbolts brothers, are testing high-speed rocket cars in the Shimmering Flats and urgently need head protection for their accident-prone test drivers. While stationed among his aerial machinery in Ironforge, the dwarven aviator Pilot Longbeard received an urgent request from the Shimmering Flats in southern Kalimdor. His friends, a pair of inventive gnomes known as the Brassbolts brothers, had taken up residence on the vast salt pans to race experimental machinery. Longbeard is tied down by military and piloting duties, leaving him unable to deliver the supplies himself. The Brassbolts' rocket car has turned out to be extraordinarily fast—so fast that their test drivers keep wiping out across the salt beds and suffering severe concussions. Longbeard procures a crate of heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets to protect their craniums. Delivering the crate gives the gnomes the leverage they need to coax reluctant pilots back behind the wheel of their volatile speed machine.

quest:1180.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Gazlowe is back to the matter you came about: the fuel regulator promised to Pozzik has not reached Ratchet. Revilgaz in Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. Gazlowe sends you to Wharfmaster Lozgil there, who can check the cargo records. Gazlowe admits he promised Pozzik a new fuel regulator and still has not received it. Revilgaz of Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. If so, there is not much to be done, but you can at least learn whether it left Booty Bay. Wharfmaster Lozgil, at the far northwestern end of the Booty Bay docks, can look through the cargo records.

quest:1181.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Wharfmaster Lozgil cannot help any further with the missing fuel regulator, and suggests you ask Baron Revilgaz himself. You will find the Baron at the tavern across the harbor in Booty Bay, on the top floor. Wharfmaster Lozgil tells you he cannot be of much more help in tracing the missing shipment bound for Ratchet. If you want to follow it up, he suggests you go to the Baron himself, since if anyone knows Revilgaz's business, it is Revilgaz. He waits in the tavern across the harbor, on the top floor.

quest:1182.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz tells you the Venture Company shredders at Lake Nazferiti in northern Stranglethorn have a new model fuel regulator that Pozzik could use. Foreman Cozzle has proven cleverer than the Baron expected, so Revilgaz sends you to find the blueprints. Baron Revilgaz explains that the Venture Company's shredders at Lake Nazferiti, in northern Stranglethorn, carry a new model of fuel regulator. Pozzik could take advantage of it if he had the details, but Cozzle, the foreman there, is cleverer than Revilgaz gave him credit for. You might have better luck. Revilgaz knows the blueprints are kept in Cozzle's house, almost certainly under lock and key. The Venture Company is based around Lake Nazferiti, in the vale's north-eastern corner. The key is with Foreman Cozzle in the cabin atop the oil tower, and the box holding the blueprints is in the small house near the tower's base. Revilgaz admits the gnome team out there is pretty good, and says the team needs every advantage it can find.

quest:1183.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz has the Fuel Regulator Blueprints ready and sends them to Pozzik on the Shimmering Flats. He gives his regards and adds that Pozzik should not hesitate to ask if he ever needs anything. Baron Revilgaz says you are all set. You carry the blueprints to Pozzik, out on the Shimmering Flats, with the Baron's regards and a message: if Pozzik ever needs anything, he should not hesitate to ask. Revilgaz says he will be waiting for news that Pozzik breaks the track record.

quest:1184.text: Parts of the Swarm. Korran has a message for Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar. You are to carry word back that Moktar is serving well out in Thousand Needles, and that Korran's studies are moving along. After the cracked carapaces taken from the silithid at the Rustmaul Digsite, Korran sends you back to Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar. Tell Belgrom that Moktar is doing his bidding well out in Thousand Needles. Tell him too that Korran's studies are progressing and that he hopes to learn more soon.

quest:1186.text: The Eighteenth Pilot. Pozzik will be busy fitting the new fuel regulator into the racer designs, but suggests that you help the team further by speaking with Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth, and likes to add modifications to the racers. Pozzik says the fuel regulator is keeping him busy, but you can help the team some more by talking to Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth in fact, and likes to add little modifications of his own to the racers. Pozzik adds that Razzeric is a little off his rocker, so you should try not to seem too surprised.

quest:1195.text: The Sacred Flame. Zangen Stonehoof sends the Horde after a sacred flame and an ancient relic. To aid Rau Cliffrunner in Thousand Needles, you seek a moonwell phial in Ashenvale. The Galak centaur guard an ancient relic in Thousand Needles. Their artifact dates to the creation of their race, and they protect it with sacred flames. Zangen Stonehoof needs water touched by lunar divinity to extinguish those flames. He sends you north to Ashenvale, where the ancestral forests hold the moonwell water he seeks. Pure moonwell water needs a vessel that will not corrupt it. You seek an etched phial from the Laughing Sisters, dryads near Raynewood Retreat. Then you submerge the phial in a moonwell along the western banks of the Falfarren River and carry it back to Mulgore.

quest:1196.text: The Sacred Flame. From Ashenvale, a phial of moonwell water travels south to Freewind Post. Rau Cliffrunner needs it to break the eternal flame guarding an ancient centaur relic in Thousand Needles. Zangen Stonehoof sends you south across central Kalimdor with an etched phial filled with purified moonwell water. You cross the sun-baked expanse of the Barrens, descend the towering Great Lift, and make for Freewind Post. Rau Cliffrunner waits on the high mesa above the canyon floor, watching the centaur clans below.

quest:1197.text: The Sacred Flame. At Splithoof Hold, Rau Cliffrunner seeks to silence the Galak centaur's sacred fire. With blessed water, you enter their stronghold, quench the brazier, and take the Cloven Hoof. North of Freewind Post, Splithoof Crag marks the heart of Galak territory in Thousand Needles. Deep in its cavern, Splithoof Hold, a fire burns that the centaur hold sacred. Rau Cliffrunner prepares an etched phial of purified water for his allies. You enter the hold, use the water to quench the flame for a moment, and take the Cloven Hoof relic guarded within.

quest:1198.text: In Search of Thaelrid. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass sends you into Blackfathom Deeps to find the scout who went missing there. The Argent Dawn fears naga and Twilight's Hammer cultists have joined forces in the flooded ruins. The Argent Dawn watches for threats across Kalimdor as well as the Scourge in Lordaeron. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass gathers reports from Darnassus about unnatural dangers. Word reaches him that naga and the doomsday zealots of the Twilight's Hammer have made a pact in Blackfathom Deeps, the flooded ruins along the Ashenvale shore. The order fears what this alliance could bring. Argent Guard Thaelrid entered the caverns to investigate the coastal rumors. Weeks have passed without word, and Shaedlass's other scouts are away on separate operations. He fears Thaelrid has fallen or been captured by the dark powers beneath the waves. Now he asks you to enter Blackfathom Deeps and bring the missing scout back alive.

quest:1199.text: Twilight Falls. At Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight's Hammer cultists join with naga beneath the Ashenvale coast. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus calls on Alliance champions to gather pendants from the fallen cultists and hinder their plans to awaken ancient evils. Beneath Ashenvale's Zoram Strand, Blackfathom Deeps lies in ruins. The night elf temple was once sacred to Elune and held a powerful moonwell, until the Sundering shattered it and plunged it beneath the sea. Now naga and cultists fill its halls. The waters have turned foul, and the cultists revere powers darker than the sea. Twilight's Hammer worships the chaotic Old Gods and seeks their return, hoping to spread madness and ruin across the world. Reports in Darnassus say the cultists have joined with the naga in Blackfathom Deeps. In the submerged halls, they perform rituals and use the temple's tainted waters to feed their dark masters' resurgence. Argent Guard Manados watches over threats to Azeroth from Darnassus on behalf of the Argent Dawn. He sees the danger in Blackfathom Deeps: its horrors could reach every civilized race. The order offers aid and recognition to heroes who enter the flooded labyrinth, cull the cultists, and bring back the Twilight Pendants from their necks as proof of their defeat.

quest:1200.text: Blackfathom Villainy. At Blackfathom Deeps, Argent Guard Thaelrid calls for the Alliance to stop Twilight Lord Kelris. The cult leader sacrifices captives to Aku'mai, and Thaelrid asks for Kelris's severed head as proof to bring to the Argent Dawn in Darnassus. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple devoted to Elune. Corruption from an ancient Old God rose through the rock, fouling the Moon Well and freeing Aku'mai, a voracious servant of that darkness. The Twilight's Hammer joined with local naga after the temple was defiled, making its holy halls a place of ritual murder. Argent Guard Thaelrid entered Blackfathom Deeps on behalf of his order, but was grievously wounded and drained of strength. Surrounded by enemies, he knows he cannot finish his mission alone. He pleads with brave Alliance travelers who reach him to kill Twilight Lord Kelris, the cultist leading sacrifices of innocents to Aku'mai in exchange for dark power.

quest:1221.text: Blueleaf Tubers. Mebok Mizzyrix seeks Blueleaf Tubers beneath the roots of Razorfen Kraul. The Ratchet goblin merchant sends trained snufflenose gophers to find and dig them up for trade. Blueleaf tubers are prized as a rare culinary delicacy across the world. They are hard to harvest because they do not grow in open fields or ordinary wild groves. Foragers find them deep underground in the southern Barrens, tangled among the roots of Razorfen Kraul. Mebok Mizzyrix, a merchant in Ratchet, devised a way to find the buried tubers. He trains snufflenose gophers, whose noses can catch a tuber's scent from fifty paces away. He supplies foragers with a command stick, a ventilated crate, and an instruction manual to guide the creatures through quilboar territory. Harvesting the tubers means entering the lands of the hostile Death's Head quilboar tribe. Foragers must guard their trained gophers from feral beasts and thorny briars in the Kraul, then command the rodents to dig up the buried bulbs. The tubers go back to Ratchet, where Mizzyrix's foreign buyers await.

quest:124.text: A Baying of Gnolls. Gnolls raid Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire from the Redridge foothills. Blackrock orcs already threaten the region, and Verner asks travelers to drive off the brutes and mystics endangering his horses. Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire has become dangerous to run. Blackrock orcs hold the heights, and gnoll packs roam the ridges around town. Gnoll raiders have reached the northern edge of Verner’s paddocks, preying on horses that wander too close to the bluffs.

quest:1241.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Stormwind, an urgent inquiry begins after a diplomat fails to reach Theramore Isle. Bishop DeLavey suspects Defias foul play and sends trusted operatives to Jorgen, a discreet contact in the Valley of Heroes. A high-ranking diplomat sailed from the Eastern Kingdoms to meet Lady Jaina Proudmoore in Theramore Isle for sensitive talks, but never arrived. Royal investigators search Stormwind for clues. The disappearance remains secret to prevent panic and keep conspirators from learning that the crown is watching. Bishop DeLavey believes the Defias Brotherhood abducted the diplomat, but does not rely only on the king’s guard. He turns to discreet contacts and seeks out Jorgen, an old acquaintance who keeps a low profile fishing in the Valley of Heroes, just inside the city gates.

quest:1242.text: The Missing Diplomat. Jorgen sends trusted operatives across Stormwind with a sealed note for Elling Trias. The delivery carries the search for the missing diplomat from the Valley of Heroes to Trias' Cheese in the Trade District. After the first inquiries into the diplomat's disappearance, Jorgen asks trusted operatives to keep silent and carry a sealed note across the city. It is meant for Trias' Cheese in Stormwind's Trade District, not a barracks or magistrate's office. The handoff avoids ordinary guard channels as concern over the missing diplomat reaches beyond the palace.

quest:1243.text: The Missing Diplomat. Elling Trias sends you south to seek news of the missing diplomat. Leads in Stormwind point toward Duskwood and Watcher Backus, a contact near Darkshire who may know of Defias activity. After a frustrating exchange with Jorgen, cheesemonger Elling Trias turns to his wider circle of informants. To save his own coin, he sends you to do the fieldwork instead of hiring agents. You carry a sealed missive across the border into Duskwood, where beasts and the undead make travel dangerous. Watcher Backus serves in the Night Watch and patrols the northern approach to Darkshire. Trias trusts him to report illicit movements through Duskwood, despite the dangers on its roads. Show Backus the sealed dispatch, and he can share guard records and local gossip about Defias Brotherhood operations in the south.

quest:1244.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Duskwood, the search for Stormwind's missing diplomat follows a lead from Watcher Backus to Defias papers at Addle's Stead. Watcher Backus of the Night Watch brings the search to Duskwood. He says an unusually large gathering of Defias bandits came to Addle's Stead several weeks ago. The bandits usually keep to themselves across the border in Westfall, so their gathering in the dark woods marks an unusual move. Now you search the abandoned farmstead for the papers they left behind.

quest:1245.text: The Missing Diplomat. You carry the recovered Defias Docket back to Stormwind as the search for a missing diplomat grows more dangerous. In Duskwood, Watcher Backus wants no part of the Defias Docket you recovered. Its papers describe plans too intricate to be simple banditry or a diversion. Afraid of royal punishment and wary of his Night Watch superiors, Backus asks you to keep his involvement quiet. The papers point to schemes dangerous enough to end careers or cost lives, so you carry them to Stormwind.

quest:1246.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Old Town, a lead in the missing diplomat's case points to a street fighter. Elling Trias sends you to find Dashel Stonefist and get answers about the suspicious papers. The investigation reaches Stormwind's rough streets. Elling Trias recalls a name tied to the coded notes and leads: Dashel Stonefist, known as Fist. He is a rough street fighter, far from the nobility around Cathedral Square. Stonefist keeps to Old Town's cramped alleys. Finding him draws the search out of Stormwind Keep's grand halls and into the city's criminal circles.

quest:1247.text: The Missing Diplomat. Dashel Stonefist has confessed in Old Town, and you carry his warning to Elling Trias. The thug names a backup abduction plot and a contact in Menethil Harbor. Dashel Stonefist gives up when he fears for his health. In an Old Town alley, he admits the conspirators' first kidnapping plan fell apart, leaving his part in the plot in ruins. To shift blame, he tells you of a secret meeting weeks ago at Addle's Stead in Duskwood. He also names one lead in their backup plan: an insider in Menethil Harbor known only as Slim.

quest:126.text: Howling in the Hills. Gnoll calls carry across the hills around Lakeshire, where Verner Osgood offers a bounty on Yowler. Stormwind's forces are stretched thin by the Blackrock orcs, leaving the town to rely on visitors against the gnolls. Gnoll cries still echo through the Redridge hills after lesser gnolls are driven from the paths around Lakeshire. Verner Osgood, the town's farrier, knows the pack will keep raiding while its leader lives. Yowler is a huge, cunning gnoll whose calls direct the pack across the hills. Verner asks for Yowler's paw as proof that the leader has been killed and the calls silenced. Stormwind's eastern border towns face danger with little help from the kingdom's army. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and disputes over the regency have paralyzed high command. Royal soldiers are focused on the Blackrock orc clans in the north, leaving Lakeshire without defenders against gnolls. Townsfolk such as Verner Osgood arrange their own bounties to keep their homes from being overrun.

quest:127.text: Selling Fish. Dockmaster Baren pays travelers to bring in spotted sunfish from Lake Everstill. The fish are a Lakeshire staple, but murlocs along the shore make them dangerous to gather. Spotted sunfish are a delicate catch prized across the lands around Lake Everstill. Townspeople and passing merchants keep demand high, yet Lakeshire's supplies often run thin despite the fish below the surface. Local threats stretch the town's strength, so even trade in basic goods depends on travelers. Anglers nearby could usually meet Dockmaster Baren's orders with ease. Now aggressive murloc tribes haunt the shallows and banks, keeping ordinary townsfolk from the water. You can fish while watching for danger, or take sunfish from the foraging murlocs that trouble the shore.

quest:1274.text: The Missing Diplomat. A quiet request in Stormwind draws you to Bishop DeLavey in Stormwind Keep. The Church and crown need help with a matter too perilous for public channels. As you travel through Stormwind, Thomas, an altar boy, approaches with a quiet request. Bishop DeLavey, a respected cleric of the Church of the Holy Light, needs an outsider's help at Stormwind Keep. He calls the matter delicate and urgent. You must keep it discreet, lest the people panic.

quest:1275.text: Researching the Corruption. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper seeks corrupted brain stems from Blackfathom Deeps. Reports say blood elves across the sea are turning to demonic magic, and he hopes to learn from the naga and satyr before history repeats itself. The ruin of their ancient kin remains a living memory to night elves across Kalimdor. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne gave in to demonic energies and became horned satyrs or serpentine naga. Now the high elves call themselves blood elves and embrace dark magic. Gershala Nightwhisper sees the old disaster taking shape again. Blackfathom Deeps offers Gershala a place to study the corruption. The temple ruins lie beneath the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, where satyr cultists and naga dwell. He asks you to gather brain stems from both, hoping to trace the link between arcane addiction, demonic corruption, and the ruin of the body.

quest:128.text: Blackrock Bounty. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon has Guard Howe offer a bounty as Blackrock forces gather in northern Redridge. Stormwind sends no royal soldiers, so the town pays independent fighters to strike at Blackrock Champions and disrupt the clan’s coordinated assault. Redridge belongs to the Kingdom of Stormwind, but the Blackrock clan ignores human borders. Orcs pour through the mountain passes from the Burning Steppes and fortify camps across northern Redridge. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and Stormwind’s regency withholds royal soldiers. With the town’s coffers dwindling, Magistrate Solomon and other local leaders offer bounties to protect Lakeshire. Guard Howe names the Blackrock Champions as the backbone of the invading vanguard. These squad leaders are battle-hardened veterans who coordinate their warbands and drive lesser grunts forward. Lakeshire’s defenders hope a bounty on the Champions will break the clan’s tactical leadership and stall a full-scale push south before the town’s outer defenses collapse.

quest:1302.text: James Hyal. "James Hyal" is an Alliance quest concerning a human settler who sailed to Kalimdor with Lady Jaina Proudmoore's expedition. After setting out to open an inn on the frontier, his family in the Eastern Kingdoms lost touch with him and seeks news of his fate through Theramore's administrative records. During the Third War, countless souls left their ancestral homes in the Eastern Kingdoms to follow Lady Jaina Proudmoore across the Great Sea. Among them was James Hyal, remembered fondly by his kin as a gifted cook. After the fighting subsided and Theramore Isle was founded, James chose to carve out a living on the rugged continent of Kalimdor by opening an inn of his own to serve travellers and fellow settlers. Back in the Eastern Kingdoms, James's brother has grown concerned after receiving no recent correspondence from across the sea. Hoping that James is merely consumed by the demands of managing a bustling roadside taproom, he asks passing travellers to track him down. The first step in finding him lies in Theramore, where Clerk Lendry oversees local records and keeps track of expedition members who have ventured out into the wilderness.

quest:133.text: Ghoulish Effigy. Abercrombie says the dead are pressing against his shack in Duskwood. He asks you to gather ghoul ribs for a grisly scarecrow meant to guard his home. Abercrombie lives beyond Darkshire's guarded bounds, alone among Duskwood's shadowed trees. Ghouls such as Flesh Eaters and Bone Chewers roam the wilds without restraint. He says ravenous corpses recently battered down his walls, and asks you for their ribs. He hopes a grisly effigy will keep the hungry dead away from his home. Abercrombie trusts a grim plan over the Night Watch or stronger walls for his wooden shack. He believes an effigy made from ghoul remains will frighten off other scavenging dead. A scarecrow built from slain undead is unsettling, yet travelers in Duskwood often do as the hermit asks for needed coin.

quest:134.text: Ogre Thieves. In western Duskwood, Abercrombie sends travelers to the ogre stronghold at Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. He says the ogres ambushed him while he foraged and took a crate of irreplaceable herbs and tools. Abercrombie, an aged hermit on the damp roads of western Duskwood, says he was attacked while gathering supplies. Brutes from the southern ogre mound drove him off, and he left behind a sturdy wooden crate packed with precious herbs and delicate instruments. The Vul'Gol Ogre Mound lies in southern Duskwood, where hostile ogres harass unwary wanderers. Abercrombie's crate rests right near the entrance, among roaring brutes and spell-weaving magi.

quest:1361.text: Regthar Deathgate. In the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate calls seasoned Horde fighters west. The veteran warrior is gathering volunteers for a campaign across the mountains into Desolace, where centaur clans terrorize the frontier. Horde leaders watch the borders for threats. In the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate has set up a defensive post guarding the western passes. Horde officers send proven adventurers west of the Crossroads to answer his call for hardened fighters. Regthar Deathgate waits in a fortified redoubt along the ridges west of the Crossroads. From there, he watches the mountain trails into Desolace. He is gathering a vanguard to cross hostile ground and strike the Kolkar and other warring centaur clans before their expansion threatens Horde territory.

quest:1362.text: The Kolkar of Desolace. The Kolkar threaten Horde lands from their stronghold in Desolace. Regthar Deathgate sends Horde champions west across the mountains to reinforce scout Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post. Centaur raiders keep pressing into the Barrens, and Regthar Deathgate knows that fighting them there will not end the threat. The Kolkar clan draws its strength from the rugged lands on Kalimdor's western coast. While their ancestral stronghold remains beyond Horde control, raiders will keep pouring through the mountain passes. To stop them, the Horde must strike at their home. Ghost Walker Post gives the Horde a foothold deep in Desolace. Scout Felgur Twocuts watches the rival centaur clans from the outpost. Regthar sends seasoned fighters from the Barrens to serve under Felgur, carrying the Horde's campaign west from defense to direct action.

quest:1365.text: Khan Dez'hepah. After The Kolkar of Desolace, Felgur Twocuts sets you against the Kolkar's leader, Khan Dez'hepah. Many centaur clans fight one another across Desolace, and Felgur wants the Kolkar disrupted before the clans unite. The Kolkar are only one of the centaur clans of Desolace. Many roam the dry plains, fighting and dying at one another's hands. Felgur Twocuts does not mind, because the centaur are strong and brutal, and a united centaur people would be a fierce foe for the Horde. They must be dealt with before that happens. Felgur's first move is to disrupt the Kolkar by killing their leader, Khan Dez'hepah. The Kolkar Village lies northeast of where Felgur stands, and Felgur wants the khan's head brought back.

quest:1366.text: Centaur Bounty. After Khan Dez'hepah, Felgur Twocuts says the scared centaur clans must now be bled. Hunt centaur of any clan across Desolace and bring Felgur fifteen of their ears. Felgur Twocuts says that now the centaur clans have been scared, it is time to bleed them. Whenever you travel Desolace, hunt centaur. Felgur does not care which clan you hunt, only that you gather ears, fifteen of them. Thinning their numbers will weaken their resolve and put an end to any thoughts of expansion.

quest:1367.text: Magram Alliance. Gurda Wildmane proposes turning the centaur clans' hatred against them: befriend one clan and use it to learn how all of them can be beaten. Siding with the Magram means slaying their enemies the Gelkis, then speaking with the Magram spokesman Warug at the edge of Magram Village, in the southeast of Desolace. Gurda Wildmane's plan is to exploit the centaurs' hatred of each other. A single clan is chosen as ally, and what it teaches shows how to defeat every clan. Choose the Magram and you cut down the Gelkis, their foes, which wins you respect among the Magram. Once you have earned enough respect, Warug, the Magram spokesman, is waiting on the outskirts of Magram Village in southeast Desolace. Before that he has nothing to say to you. The Magram have no words for the weak and kill them instead, so he sends you off to prove your strength against many Gelkis.

quest:1368.text: Gelkis Alliance. Gurda Wildmane proposes turning the centaur clans' hatred against them: befriend one clan and use it to learn how all of them can be beaten. Siding with the Gelkis means killing their worst enemy, the Magram, then meeting Uthek the Wise, a shaman of the Gelkis, on the edge of Gelkis Village in the southwest of Desolace. Gurda Wildmane's plan is to exploit the centaurs' hatred of each other. A single clan is chosen as ally, and what it teaches shows how to defeat every clan. Choose the Gelkis and you kill the Magram, whom the Gelkis hate most, to win their respect. Once you have won their respect, Uthek the Wise, shaman of the Gelkis, is to be met on the outskirts of Gelkis Village in southwest Desolace. Before then you are not welcome there: Uthek says you tread on Gelkis earth, and friendship must be proven by killing Magram centaur. Come back once Magram blood has soaked the ground.

quest:1369.text: Broken Tears. Warug says the Gelkis foolishly believe the centaur mother, Theradras, protects them. He sends you into the cave in their village to destroy the crystals they hoard there, the tears of Theradras, and bring him three of the broken pieces. Warug scorns the Gelkis for trusting Theradras, mother of the centaur, to protect them. To him no one protects the centaur, and the Magram, being the strongest, need no protection. He sends you to the cave in the Gelkis village, where they keep a hoard of crystals called the tears of Theradras. Smash them and bring Warug three broken pieces. He will only trust you with this if you are no enemy of the Magram.

quest:1370.text: Stealing Supplies. Uthek the Wise says meat gives the Gelkis their strength, and that the Magram keep extra stores so they can fight longer between hunts. You are sent to raid the Magram village to the east and bring back six bags of dried meat. Between wars the Gelkis hunt, because meat means strength and a full belly fights harder than an empty one. Uthek the Wise says the Magram keep spare stock to last them between hunts. Raid their village to the east, take those stores, and their strength will fail. Six bags of crudely dried meat are wanted, to be brought to Uthek at the Gelkis Village.

quest:1371.text: Gizmo for Warug. Warug, in the Magram Village, remembers a gnome who once came to Desolace with a cart of strange things. He kept a wooden human from that cart until he broke it, and now he wants a new one: an advanced target dummy. A little gnome once came to Desolace, long ago, with horses and a cart. The cart held curious things: some burned in different colors, others moved though they were not alive. Warug killed the gnome, but first the gnome made him laugh. Warug kept his favorite thing from the cart, a human made of wood that waved at him until he hit it and broke it. Now he wants a new one, an advanced target dummy, and expects it from anyone who is no enemy of the Magram.

quest:1373.text: Ongeku. Uthek the Wise of the Gelkis says you still have more to prove, and that for now the Gelkis will take on the Magram without your help. The earth has whispered to Uthek of draenethyst, and you are sent far away to the Swamp of Sorrows for a shard held by the lost one Ongeku. After Stealing Supplies, Uthek the Wise tells you that your next undertaking lies a long way off. Those who listen hear many secrets in the earth, and one Uthek has heard is of a red crystal called draenethyst, newly arrived in this land and brought from a place of flying mountains and ruling demons. A shard of it, Uthek says, will make the magic strong. The lost one Ongeku holds a shard in the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. When you return, Uthek will look for proof that the Gelkis can still call you friend.

quest:1374.text: Khan Jehn. Following Ongeku, Uthek the Wise tells you the earth says the Magram are growing weak, and that the hour has come to slay their Khan. Uthek wants the head of Khan Jehn brought to Gelkis Village. Uthek the Wise at Gelkis Village says the earth speaks to Uthek, and it tells of the Magram growing weak. Uthek names their Khan, Jehn, as the one to strike down and asks for the head of the Magram Khan. Uthek expects you to still count as a friend of the Gelkis when you come back.

quest:1375.text: Khan Shaka. Warug of the Magram, pleased with your help after Gizmo for Warug, now wants the head of Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis. He means to stare at it and laugh at his enemy. In Magram Village, Warug tells you that you have helped the Magram and he likes you. Now he wants you to kill Khan Shaka, the Khan of the Gelkis, and bring him the head. He says he wants to stare at it and laugh at him. He expects you to stay on good terms with the Magram.

quest:1382.text: Strange Alliance. Captain Pentigast sees luck in the way the centaur clans of Desolace fight each other, since as one force they could not be stopped. The Gelkis are locked in brutal war with the Magram, so Pentigast sends you to Uthek the Wise in southwestern Desolace to seek an alliance. Captain Pentigast counts it good fortune that the centaur clans war on one another, for joined together they could not be stopped. Pentigast wants to push that edge. The Gelkis and Magram are locked in brutal war, so striking at the Magram might win the Gelkis over. Uthek the Wise can be found where the Gelkis camps begin, in the southwest of Desolace, and through her an alliance might be struck. She turns you away at first, telling you to leave and to return after killing many Magram.

quest:1384.text: Raid on the Kolkar. After Strange Alliance, Uthek the Wise sends you against the Kolkar centaurs to the northeast. Kill them, take their charms, and bring ten of those charms back to Uthek. Uthek scoffs at the Kolkar centaurs for thinking their magic strong; in Uthek's view they know nothing of magic. You go northeast to the Kolkar, kill them, and take their charms. Uthek wants ten Crude Charms to throw in the fire, laughing as they burn.

quest:1385.text: Brutal Politics. Captain Pentigast believes whichever centaur clan wins the wars of Desolace will spill out and threaten the Alliance strongholds. To learn how to beat them, Pentigast wants an alliance with one clan: fight the Gelkis, win over the Magram, and speak with Warug. War rages across Desolace, centaur against centaur, and the Alliance believes the winner will spill out against its strongholds. That cannot be allowed. To learn how to beat the centaurs, Captain Pentigast says, the Alliance needs one of the clans as a friend. The Magram fight the Gelkis, so striking at the Gelkis might make the Magram weigh an alliance. Earn their favor, then go to Warug in the Magram village, in Desolace's southeast. Warug warns that to be a friend of the Magram, you must kill Gelkis.

quest:1386.text: Assault on the Kolkar. After Brutal Politics, Warug in Magram Village wants proof that you can kill Kolkar the way the Magram do. Head north and slay Kolkar centaurs, scouts and maulers. Warug sneers that the Kolkar believe themselves strong while the Magram laugh at them as they kill them. Warug wants you to prove you can kill Kolkar as the Magram do, so you head north: twelve Kolkar centaurs, twelve scouts and six maulers are to fall.

quest:1387.text: Centaur Bounty. Corporal Melkins at Nijel's Point says every centaur clan in Desolace shares one trait, cruelty, and that peace will not come while the centaur remain. Melkins asks you to hunt them across the land and bring fifteen of their ears. At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins describes a centaur race split among many clans, each with a leader and plans of its own, yet alike in cruelty. Peace, Melkins says, will only come if the centaurs are removed. Wandering Desolace, you hunt centaur and take their ears. Melkins wants a great many, fifteen in all, and calls the work a service to the Alliance that brings the war's end nearer.

quest:1394.text: Final Passage. Parqual Fintallas tells you that you have passed this test and the ones before it. You are sent back to Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles, who will sense the change in you and see whether you have grown strong in mind, body and spirit, enough to be honoured for your efforts. This is the last step of the Test of Faith, the chain of trials that Dorn Plainstalker began. Dorn waits in the Weathered Nook, in a cave reached by a ramp, north of Freewind Post. Parqual Fintallas urges you to stay true to the balance you have shown throughout these trials.

quest:1431.text: Alliance Relations. Thrall seeks a careful hand to preserve peace with the Alliance. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok sends seasoned Horde adventurers to find Keldran near the western exit. The work calls for quiet diplomacy and intelligence to protect Thrall’s fragile peace. Thrall knows war with the Alliance could ruin his young nation. Raised in human captivity, the Warchief learned human statecraft and military strategy. Craven Drok watches for warriors and champions with patience for a subtler path, one that looks beyond raw force. Near Orgrimmar’s western exit, Keldran keeps a humble dwelling. He practices magic and covert arts, working with appearances, perception, and statecraft. Keldran seeks discreet operatives to serve the Warchief as the Horde faces a tense standoff with its bitter rivals.

quest:1432.text: Alliance Relations. In Orgrimmar, Alliance advances across Kalimdor raise fears of dangerous political fallout. The Horde sends orders to Desolace to purge demons before the Alliance can accuse Thrall's people of renewed ties to the Burning Legion. Alliance scouts and expeditions crossing Kalimdor put the Horde in a delicate position. Demonic remnants across central Kalimdor could confirm old suspicions that the orcs and their allies still serve the Burning Legion. With Warchief Thrall's sanction, Keldran oversees operations from Orgrimmar to clear those remnants before hostile Alliance factions can use them to justify war. Orders south lead through the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains and into Desolace. Just north of the vast Kodo Graveyard stands Ghost Walker Post. Horde agents such as Takata Steelblade watch the wastes, where rampant centaur tribes and spreading demonic corruption both threaten the region.

quest:1437.text: Vahlarriel's Search. Vahlarriel Demonslayer has come to Desolace to learn what became of two missing nobles of House Malem, a Darnassian merchant family. Their father fears the worst, and the last word of the pair places them in the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks back. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon. Vahlarriel Demonslayer is looking for Tyranis and Dalinda Malem, whose father fears the worst and has charged Vahlarriel with doing everything possible to find them. The search has barely begun, and Vahlarriel hopes it will not keep them in Desolace long. The pair were last reported crossing the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks ago. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon in Desolace and to come at once when you do. Its charred remains lie there, with a chest among them.

quest:1438.text: Vahlarriel's Search. After the second part of Vahlarriel's Search, Vahlarriel Demonslayer sends you to look for Dalinda and Tyranis Malem, beginning at the fortress. Word of it goes to Vahlarriel's superiors in Darnassus, who worry about Tyranis's motives and want Dalinda brought home safe above all. Vahlarriel Demonslayer wants you to look for both Dalinda and Tyranis, beginning at the fortress, and return with what you learn. Vahlarriel will contact superiors in Darnassus right away. A private word follows: they worry about why Tyranis came to Desolace, and they care most that Dalinda gets home safe. As for Tyranis, they want him gauged first, before any homecoming.

quest:1439.text: Search for Tyranis. Dalinda Malem tells you the orcs slaughtered all their guards and servants before bringing her and Tyranis here. Tyranis tried to speak to them, and she cannot leave until she knows what has become of her brother. She asks you to find him and come back when his fate is known. Dalinda tells you that orcs killed every guard and servant of theirs before dragging her and Tyranis to this place. She expected to die at once, yet the orcs clearly had other designs. Tyranis tried talking to them, perhaps hoping his arcane learning would impress them, though she cannot say why. She will not escape until she knows his fate, so she asks you to find him and return when you do. He is in a building left of the fortress entrance. Dalinda dreads that Tyranis, if allowed, will seek the Burning Blade's secrets and become one of them. Power has always drawn him, as it does anyone magic seduces. To her people even studying such things is a grave crime, and she doubts she could face her family with word that his spirit toyed with that danger.

quest:1440.text: Return to Vahlarriel. Dalinda Malem is ready to leave Thunder Axe Fortress. She thanks you for what you have done for her and her family, and says the time is yours to choose. You escort her out, then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer. Dalinda asks whether the time has come, and offers thanks for all you have done for her and her family, in case things do not go as hoped. If you are ready, nothing else keeps her here, and she will go when you judge the moment right. You escort her out of Thunder Axe Fortress and then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer in Desolace.

quest:1442.text: Seeking the Kor Gem. You cross the sea to Darkshore in search of a Kor gem for Jordan Stilwell. Thundris Windweaver sends an Alliance paladin initiate into Blackfathom Deeps, where naga corrupt the potent stone. Jordan needs it for his craft. Paladins in training cross continental borders to Darkshore for materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell. In Auberdine, the night elf Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Night elves keep their distance, and some fallen humans have betrayed their trust, yet Thundris still believes paladins can follow a righteous path. He tells them where ancient gems can be found. Blackfathom Deeps lies beneath the foggy northwestern coast of Ashenvale. Twilight's Hammer cultists and treacherous sea-dwellers inhabit its submerged halls. Naga priestesses there channel foul magic through ancient Kor gems. The gem you seek is deep within the temple complex, amid its dark halls and dangerous inhabitants.

quest:1454.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor tells you of Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck his ship in the northwest waters of Desolace, and he left a valuable chest behind and teleported away. The chest and what is inside are to be found. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor tells you of a first order of business. It concerns Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck Karnitol's ship in the northwest waters of Desolace. Karnitol and his servants tried to carry one of his costlier chests to shore, but the giants swarmed in, and he gave up the chest and teleported himself and his servants out. The chest and its contents are to be found, then returned to Karnitol in Stormwind. It lies along the northern coastline, in the Ethel Rethor stretch.

quest:1455.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. The chest of the mage Karnitol has been pried open, and it is completely empty. Long, deep scratches on its sides and top suggest neither man nor giant was responsible, and you return to Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point. You study what forced the chest open. Long, deep scratches run along its sides and top. They point to something that was neither man nor giant, and they do not look like the work of a dagger or sword. The chest is completely empty. With nothing else to be done, you close it and prepare to leave, knowing Kreldig Ungor will be disappointed.

quest:1456.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor still thinks Karnitol's belongings can be found. Up the same coast, by Ranazjar Isle, the Slitherblade naga hold a place among night elf ruins that lie at the bottom of the sea, and Kreldig reckons the satchel is most likely there. Following the second part of the Karnitol shipwreck search, Kreldig Ungor tells you hope is not lost. Along the same coast but farther north, close to Ranazjar Isle, sunken night elf ruins lie on the ocean floor, and the Slitherblade naga call them home. Kreldig judges it the likeliest place for Karnitol's satchel. A Recovery Diver's Potion is provided. Kreldig figures a scouting party that came so far south had to be a strong one. So in looking for Karnitol's belongings, Kreldig would try the more powerful naga first, the tidehunters and the sea witches.

quest:1457.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor sends you to Ironforge with Karnitol's satchel, to put it in the hands of Roetten Stonehammer, who will pay you for the work. Kreldig Ungor tells you to carry Karnitol's things back to Roetten Stonehammer in Ironforge, who will pay you for the work. With a laugh, Kreldig adds that Roetten may be so pleased that you get asked to join the Reclaimers full time. The way back should be made carefully and without dawdling, since Karnitol has little patience, though he is a generous man.

quest:1458.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor is gathering reagents for the gnome mage Leftwitch, who lives in Kharanos, and the Reclaimers are short-handed. He wants claws and horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east before the rest of the list can begin. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor has another job on his hands: fetching reagents for Leftwitch, the gnome mage who lives in Kharanos. Roetten reckons it is easy coin, since the Reclaimers are already out in Desolace, and Kreldig says he does not care that the crew is short-handed. The first items on the list should be simple enough. Kreldig wants ten claws and ten horns taken from the Hatefury satyrs to the east, who are found in the Sargeron ruins due east of Nijel's Point. Once he has them, the rest of the list can begin.

quest:1459.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Next on Leftwitch's list for Kreldig Ungor is venom from the scorpashi and hides from aged kodo. Kreldig cannot say where to find either, since he does not know Desolace well. Following the first part of Leftwitch's list, Kreldig Ungor turns to the next items. They look simple enough, but the instructions are exact. The mage wants venom from the scorpashi, any of them will do, and hides from kodo, but only aged kodo. Dying and ancient kodo are no use. Kreldig wants seven vials of venom and three hides. Mages, Kreldig muses, ask for some odd things. Kreldig has no idea where the kodo and the scorpashi roam. Kreldig barely knows the area and has had no time to explore it.

quest:1465.text: Vahlarriel's Search. Going on with the search of the Malems' wagon, you turn up a pendant and a trail of footprints heading south. Smoke rises from a big fort far off. Vahlarriel Demonslayer at Nijel's Point should be shown the pendant and told about the sign that the Malems may live. Searching the wagon further, you turn up a pendant, and beyond it footprints leading south. Far off, smoke rises from a big fort. A tended fire makes it, not buildings burning, and your instincts say that if the Malems are still alive, they were taken that way. Vahlarriel Demonslayer at Nijel's Point should see the Malem Pendant, and should hear of the footprints leading south.

quest:1472.text: Devourer of Souls. In the Undercity's Temple of the Damned, Carendin Halgar guides Forsaken warlocks toward binding a succubus. Godrick Farsan knows how to lure one from the Twisting Nether with the hearts of pure, loving mortals. Carendin Halgar teaches that a succubus must be enticed across the threshold, not summoned by command. The demon hungers to ruin virtue and consume mortal essence. To draw it forth, you offer the hearts of genuinely virtuous, loving men as bait. Halgar sends you to Godrick Farsan, who knows where such rare quarry can be found. Deeper in the Temple of the Damned, Godrick Farsan helps Carendin prepare for demonic binding. Farsan has lost his physical eyesight, but says this grants him a deeper sight. He claims to perceive spiritual currents and distant souls with uncanny clarity, and can guide you to the pure hearts needed to draw out the demon.

quest:1474.text: The Binding. In the Undercity, an initiate faces the rite that grants command of a succubus. Carendin Halgar directs the warlock to use Pure Hearts to draw a demon from the Twisting Nether into a ritual circle, then master it through combat. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks hone their command of demons. Summoning a succubus marks a critical passage in their training. A voidwalker relies on brute force, and an imp on lesser malice, but a succubus can ensnare its summoner with seductive and mental enchantments. Carendin Halgar demands that each initiate prove mind and magic unshakable before he entrusts them with lasting dominion over such a demon.

quest:1476.text: Hearts of the Pure. In the Undercity, Godrick Farsan assigns a warlock trial on Carendin Halgar’s behalf. To prepare bait for a succubus, you hunt two righteous human men; their pure hearts are an irresistible temptation to the demon. Carendin Halgar, master summoner in the Temple of the Damned, assigns Godrick Farsan the groundwork for binding a succubus. Succubi prey on desire and ruin, yet untainted virtue draws them from the Twisting Nether, ripe for corruption. Godrick scours human lands for souls whose goodness remains pristine and unbroken. Godrick Farsan names two men whose virtue marks them for sacrifice. Dalin Forgewright cares for desperate Lordaeron refugees barred from sanctuary outside the sealed Greymane Wall in southern Silverpine. Comar Villard searches the perilous marshlands of the Wetlands tirelessly for any trace of his lost wife. Their devotion, empathy, and loyalty make them prime sacrifices to a Forsaken warlock.

quest:148.text: Supplies from Darkshire. Abercrombie in western Duskwood asks travelers to fetch a rare thread from Darkshire. The hermit claims he is too frail to cross the haunted woods and asks for Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva. North of Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie lives alone in a shack in western Duskwood. He tells travelers that age and frailty keep him from making the dangerous journey through the woods to buy goods in Darkshire. His request seems simple: go to the township's town square and speak with Madame Eva for a spool of Ghost Hair Thread.

quest:1480.text: The Corrupter. A piece of flayed demon skin, taken from the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress, smells rotten yet is surprisingly pliable. Red markings of some language cover one side, and at the bottom is a clear symbol that looks like a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may be able to tell you more. The torn skin stinks of rot, yet it bends easily, though it seems dry and fragile. Unrolled, it carries red markings on one side, a written language of some sort. At the bottom is a plain symbol, which you take to be a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may know more about the skin. Maurin holds that the Burning Blade are coming to see how weak they are, with poor magic and little strength. Whatever power they have comes from those they serve, not from any grasp of true power and knowledge.

quest:1481.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, but first any wards the creature holds against scrying must be broken. For that, Maurin wants the scalp of a Hatefury shadowstalker, hunted in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, given the proper reagents. If the lord is as powerful as Maurin suspects, those must come from deadly creatures, and Maurin is sure you, acting in the Warchief's name, will take up the challenge. The first need is to break any wards the demon has against scrying. For that Maurin wants a scalp from a satyr, though only a Hatefury shadowstalker's will serve. They are to be sought in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast, near Sargeron. Maurin cautions you against bringing back the wrong scalp. The wrong reagents could get people killed, since the demon lord may carry contingency spells meant to slay anyone who tries to scry on him. Maurin adds that fate has already dealt out enough pain.

quest:1482.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter wants an oracle crystal, which the naga craft for their oracles, in order to find the demon lord Azrethoc. A vast coral reef lies northwest along the coast, home to the Slitherblade naga, and they will not welcome you. Maurin Bonesplitter says an oracle crystal will do the job of finding the demon lord Azrethoc, whose signature was on the skin you brought. Naga craft such crystals, and their oracles use them. Up the coast to the northwest lies a vast coral reef which the naga have made their home while near the shore, and the oracles can be found in that place. The Slitherblade there are deadly and will take your intrusion badly, so Maurin urges you to go carefully and quickly. Maurin points out that finding and destroying Lord Azrethoc would earn both of you much favor with the Warchief. Working together, and swiftly, would serve the ends of each.

quest:1483.text: Ziz Fizziks. On the western ridge of Windshear Crag, Ziz Fizziks has left the Venture Company for the Tinkers' Union. A gnome engineer's arrival drove him away, though his new superior works him just as hard. The Venture Company brought Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a gnome engineer, into its employ, and Ziz Fizziks took it as an insult. He could not bear working beside a gnomish rival, so he looked for a way out. Ziz contacted Sputtervalve, who represented the Tinkers' Union, and begged for a transfer away from Gerenzo's oversight. The Tinkers' Union gave Ziz Fizziks a new position, but not the easy life he expected. On the western edge of Windshear Crag, he found that Sputtervalve drove him as hard as any Venture Company foreman. Still, Ziz would rather labor under a demanding goblin superior than share an engineering workshop with a gnome.

quest:1484.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter has found the demon lord far more dangerous than expected. He is certain Takata Steelblade doubts his abilities, and leaving the swordsman uninformed of what happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin sends you to speak with Takata, who is nearby. Maurin Bonesplitter finds the creature much more dangerous than he had anticipated. No doubt Takata Steelblade questions whether Maurin can handle it, and not being told of what just happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin asks you to speak to the swordsman and offer to slay the demon, should Takata allow it. Maurin cautions you not to press Takata too hard, since it is better if Takata believes the idea is his own. Takata Steelblade is close at hand, just across the path from Maurin, on a cliff overlooking the Kodo Graveyard.

quest:1487.text: Deviate Eradication. Deviate Eradication is a task assigned by the night elf druid Ebru above the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. While other disciples focus on waking their slumbering leader, Ebru asks adventurers to purge the caverns of mutated deviate beasts spawned by his twisted vision. Ridding the subterranean oasis of these horrors is an essential step in stemming the corruption threatening the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex brought his followers to the subterranean springs of the Barrens with an ambitious vision: tap into the Emerald Dream to regrow the parched plains into a lush, thriving woodland. Instead, Naralex became ensnared within the Dream, his slumber twisting into an agonizing nightmare. Rather than healing the land, the power surging through the caverns warped the native wildlife and plant life into monstrous, aggressive mutants known as deviate beasts. Perched in the cliff-face cavern overlooking the cave entrance, Ebru and a handful of surviving Disciples of Naralex watch in despair as their numbers dwindle. While some among them dedicate their energy toward awakening their fallen master, Ebru recognizes an immediate crisis. Left unchecked, the rapidly multiplying deviate vipers, shamblers, ravagers, and dreadfangs will spill outward into the Barrens. Ebru therefore recruits passing adventurers to descend into the deep tunnels and cull the aberrant monstrosities at their source.

quest:149.text: Ghost Hair Thread. Madame Eva seeks ghost hair in the hills south of Darkshire. She needs the strands to spin Ghost Hair Thread for Abercrombie, and sends travelers to find Blind Mary at an abandoned farmhouse. An ethereal comb lets them gather hair from the tormented spirit. Madame Eva needs ghost hair to spin thread for Abercrombie. Linen and wool cannot serve the rituals of Duskwood, so she gives you a Spectral Comb to gather strands from a spirit. It can pass through the veil of death and catch loose spectral hair without violence. South of Darkshire, Blind Mary haunts an abandoned farmhouse. The tormented spirit despairs over her appearance and screams at intruders to look away. In anguish over what she had become, she tore out her own eyes. The Spectral Comb offers a brief comfort: she can groom her ghostly hair, though her torment continues.

quest:150.text: Murloc Poachers. Along Lake Everstill, Murloc Poachers are stripping Lakeshire's waters of fish. Dockmaster Baren needs you to thin their swelling ranks before the town loses its main food supply. Dockmaster Baren needs you to protect the fish that feed Lakeshire. Lake Everstill supplies the mountain town and its market with fresh catches. Large tribes of murlocs now crowd the shallows and scour the waters for food. Left unchecked, they could wipe out the local fish and leave Lakeshire without its main food supply. Murlocs usually scavenge along the coast, so their numbers high in the Redridge Mountains are hard to explain. Dockmaster Baren wonders why they have come so far from the open ocean.
