quest:303.text: The Dark Iron War. At Dun Modr, on the Wetlands' northern edge, Motley Garmason leads a desperate defense. The Dark Iron clan holds the town after saboteurs shattered the Thandol Span, leaving the Ironforge Mountaineers with a tenuous line as they wait for reinforcements that may never come. Dun Modr guarded the southern end of the colossal Thandol Span, the bridge linking Khaz Modan to Lordaeron. Dark Iron saboteurs and demolitionists shattered its archway, severing Alliance travel before they overran the stronghold. Motley Garmason and a handful of surviving defenders withdrew to an observation camp just outside town. Without a counterattack, the northern gateway risks permanent Dark Iron dominion. Dwarven regiments are deployed to distant Alliance battlefields, leaving Motley's small detachment largely to fend for itself. His scouts try to signal Ironforge for relief, but communications falter and promised reserves remain out of sight. To buy time and disrupt the enemy's entrenchments, Motley orders surgical strikes into Dun Modr's ruins. The aim is to thin the ranks of Dark Iron engineers, tunnelers, and front-line soldiers before they push farther south into the Wetlands.

quest:304.text: A Grim Task. Longbraid the Grim seeks vengeance in the Wetlands after Dun Modr falls. The Dark Iron assault shattered the Thandol Span and took the lives of his brother and many soldiers. Now he wants Balgaras the Foul slain, with the warlock's ear as proof. The northern Wetlands are scarred by fighting between Ironforge Mountaineers and Dark Iron infiltrators. Dun Modr fell during the siege, and the western bridge of the Thandol Span was shattered. Longbraid the Grim lost many loyal soldiers and his brother in the assault. He wants the Dark Iron clan to pay for those deaths. Scouts such as Roggo have found that Balgaras the Foul commands the Dark Iron force occupying Dun Modr. The warlock hides while ordering his soldiers to carry out his dark designs. Longbraid hopes Balgaras's death will break the force's resolve and let Ironforge's survivors secure the passage north.

quest:305.text: In Search of The Excavation Team. Tarrel Rockweaver waits in the Wetlands for word from Merrin at the Whelgar Excavation Site. His wife has missed two weeks of letters, and he fears disaster at the eastern dig. Tarrel Rockweaver has heard nothing from his wife, Merrin, for two weeks. From her post at the Whelgar Excavation Site, she used to send him weekly letters about the work. Now Tarrel fears calamity has struck the camp. With dwarf authorities stretched thin, he turns to passing scouts to learn whether the diggers are still alive. The Whelgar Excavation Site lies east in the Wetlands, where dwarves dig for ancient Titan relics and history. Crews working in the wild can face beasts and threats from below. The site is far from the main roads, and whatever stopped the letters has left the diggers beyond easy reach.

quest:306.text: In Search of The Excavation Team. Merrin Rockweaver sends word from the Whelgar's Excavation site after mottled raptors overrun the dig. Her letter tells Tarrel Rockweaver that she survived, while most of the expedition did not. Merrin Rockweaver has a report for you from the ridge above Whelgar's Excavation site. The team was uncovering rare artifacts and massive prehistoric fossils when packs of mottled raptors swept through the dig. Most of the crew died in the attack. Merrin and the other survivors remain cut off from Menethil Harbor. At Menethil Harbor, Tarrel Rockweaver learns that his wife survived with at least two companions. Ormer's courage helped them escape, easing Tarrel's fear. The deaths of so many colleagues still weigh on the town and its frontier spirit.

quest:3099.text: Tainted Scroll. The Tainted Scroll is an early quest in Deathknell that directs newly awakened Forsaken warlocks to their trainer, Maximillion. Through this missive, Maximillion invites the initiate to embrace power and dark servitude as a means of securing genuine freedom. Shortly after newly risen Forsaken begin clearing out mindless Scourge remnants around Deathknell, an ominous missive arrives bearing the seal of Maximillion, the local warlock trainer. The scroll beckons the recipient to contemplate the nature of servitude and autonomy before returning to the ruined settlement to speak with him directly.

quest:3100.text: Simple Letter. The Simple Letter is an introductory directive that guides novice warriors to trainer Llane Beshere at Northshire Abbey. It marks the beginning of their formal martial instruction and urges them to assist the troubled citizens of the valley. The Simple Letter serves as an initial introduction for aspiring warriors arriving in Northshire Valley. Directed to Llane Beshere, the resident warrior trainer at Northshire Abbey, the letter prompts newly arrived fighters to make contact with their instructor, familiarize themselves with their surroundings, and prepare for the demands of martial life. Although Northshire Abbey enjoys protection under the watchful presence of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the peaceful facade of the valley belies deeper trouble. As Beshere notes upon receiving the letter, the surrounding residents face numerous plights that require able-bodied protectors, urging fresh recruits to master their weapons and step forward in defense of the realm.

quest:3101.text: Consecrated Letter. The Consecrated Letter is an introductory summons carried by initiates of the Holy Light arriving in Northshire Valley. It directs the bearer to report to their class trainer at Northshire Abbey to begin their training and embrace their role as a visible symbol of faith. The Consecrated Letter marks the formal beginning of an initiate's journey in Northshire Valley. Addressed to newly arrived wielders of the Holy Light, the document calls the bearer to seek out their trainer at Northshire Abbey to formalize their instruction and accept their responsibilities within the Kingdom of Stormwind. Upon presenting the letter, the initiate is reminded of the weight carried by their vocation. The Holy Light shines visibly within those who channel it, making them immediate symbols of hope to allies and clear targets for their adversaries. The trainer emphasizes that such power demands disciplined conduct and an awareness of one's public example. Beyond spiritual obligations, the letter establishes an ongoing relationship between student and mentor. As the initiate tests their mettle against the local threats confronting Northshire, they are expected to return regularly to the abbey grounds to unlock deeper understandings of combat and divine grace.

quest:320.text: Return to Bellowfiz. Return to Bellowfiz is a short delivery quest in Dun Morogh where an adventurer brings a cask of local Evershine to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It concludes a local favor, rewarding the thirsty driver with a welcome drink. Return to Bellowfiz is an errand in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. After aiding with local hunting, an adventurer receives a freshly brewed cask of Evershine with instructions to carry it straight to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It is a straightforward favor that highlights the informal camaraderie and mutual support that keep the cold frontier running. Steelgrill's Depot serves as a busy center of mechanical testing, vehicle maintenance, and gnomish craft just outside Kharanos. For pilots stationed out in the freezing winds, nothing hits the spot quite like a draught of strong local drink. Pilot Bellowfiz wastes no time upon delivery, eager to uncork a bottle on the spot and enjoy the fruits of local labor.

quest:321.text: Lightforge Iron. In Menethil Harbor, Glorin Steelbrow seeks the lost cargo of an elven destroyer. The Flying Osprey carried rare Lightforge iron when it sank with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras during the Second War. The Flying Osprey sailed from Lordaeron with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras. The elven destroyer carried a precious cargo of Lightforge iron and traveled beside the fleet for safety. But the Dragonmaw clan's enslaved red dragons swept down from the sky. They set the fleet ablaze, sending sailors and sanctified metal beneath the waves.

quest:322.text: Blessed Arm. In Stormwind, Blessed Arm carries lightforge iron toward a weapon against Morbent Fel. After salvaging the ingots from the wreck of the Flying Osprey in the Wetlands, you bring the precious metal to master dwarven smith Grimand Elmore, who can shape it to face the necromancer. Glorin Steelbrow packs the recovered lightforge iron for Stormwind. The metal is rare, and its power against foul and unholy beings demands a smith who knows how to work it. After the shipment came from the wreck of the Flying Osprey off the Wetlands coast, Glorin knew of only one artisan in the southern kingdoms suited to the task: master weaponsmith Grimand Elmore. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Grimand Elmore keeps one of the city's finest anvils. Years have passed since he last hammered lightforge iron, he says, when you bring him the recovered shipment. The veteran artisan is intrigued by the chance to strike at the necromancer Morbent Fel, and agrees to put his hammer to work.

quest:323.text: Proving Your Worth. In Duskwood, Sven Yorgen tests your strength before he lets you face Morbent Fel. The hermit seeks revenge for his family and needs proof you can overcome the undead at Raven Hill Cemetery. At a secluded camp north of the howling woods, Sven Yorgen grieves for his family and burns with fury over their slaughter. He has learned that the Dark Riders who destroyed his homestead were allied with the necromancer Morbent Fel. Sven wants revenge, but he will not send an untried ally straight into Fel's grasp. First, he asks you to prove your combat skill against the skeletal forces at Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery lies south of Forlorn Rowe, and its grounds and mausoleum crawl with corpses bound by Fel's magic. Skeletal Raiders patrol among the tombstones with swords, while Skeletal Warders and Healers tend the chambers below. To earn Sven's trust, you must push deep into the necropolis and clear this vanguard. Mor'Ladim, a vengeful phantom, prowls the cemetery paths.

quest:324.text: The Lost Ingots. Glorin Steelbrow needs Lightforge iron from a shipwreck off the Wetlands. The chest holds only one ingot, and the Bluegill murlocs have taken the rest. The Flying Osprey lies broken off the Wetlands shore. Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven priest, sent you to recover its Lightforge iron. The waterlogged chest in the cargo hold holds only a single ingot. Bluegill murlocs near the wreck have scavenged the rest of the shipment. Lightforge iron is rare metal suited to sacred smithing. Glorin Steelbrow needs it for a weapon, so the bars cannot be left in Bluegill camps. Hunt the Bluegill raiders in the shallows near the broken hull and reclaim the scattered ingots for Glorin.

quest:325.text: Armed and Ready. You carry Morbent's Bane back to Sven Yorgen, the weapon forged to strip away Morbent Fel's unholy defenses. Morbent Fel's hold over Raven Hill cemetery resists ordinary steel. Blades shatter or glance off the dark wards around the necromancer. A weapon made to break those wards is now ready. Grimand Elmore shaped the metal in Stormwind's Dwarven District, and sacred power consecrated it. Morbent's Bane can now sever Fel's tie to unlife.

quest:328.text: The Hidden Key. Tucked away in the binding of Bookie Herod's ledgers is a small brass key alongside notes referencing a secure strongbox. Locating this container deep within the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound may reveal how Private Thorsen was betrayed. Searching through Bookie Herod's ledgers yields no direct mention of Private Thorsen, but it reveals something else: a small brass key concealed inside a book's binding. Scraps among the paperwork make passing mention of a secure strongbox tucked away inside the Stockpile, the cavern complex at the rear of Kurzen's Compound. Opening that container might reveal how Thorsen's cover was blown. Reaching the strongbox requires delving into the cave system behind the compound. Heavy, bronze-bound, and sturdily constructed, the chest sits among stacked crates in the cave.

quest:329.text: The Spy Revealed!. Inside Bookie Herod's strongbox lies a damp piece of parchment detailing the daily routines of Private Thorsen. Bearing only the initial M, this correspondence suggests an informant has embedded themselves among the rebels in northern Stranglethorn Vale. The muddy note is meant for Lieutenant Doren. Opening the strongbox reveals not just valuables, but an itinerary tracking Private Thorsen. The barely legible writing recounts his patrol routes, his companions, and his daily activities around the Rebel Camp, marked only with the signature -M. Such detailed observations could only come from someone living alongside Thorsen, pointing to a traitor within the rebel camp.

quest:330.text: Patrol Schedules. Following the discovery of an incriminating message signed only by an initial, Lieutenant Doren seeks to identify the traitor within the Rebel Camp. By cross-referencing duty rosters, duty records can reveal who shared patrol routes with Private Thorsen during the previous week. The recovered note bears only the initial M, which provides little on its own to expose the conspirator aiding the Kurzen forces. However, the author mentions sharing regular duty paths alongside Private Thorsen throughout the previous week. Lieutenant Doren directs you across the Rebel Camp to speak with Corporal Sethman, the soldier responsible for maintaining duty logs, to identify who walked alongside Thorsen.

quest:331.text: Report to Doren. After obtaining the patrol information, Corporal Sethman directs you back to Lieutenant Doren. Delivering these findings brings crucial military intelligence directly to the rebels' commander in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Corporal Sethman reminds you that Lieutenant Doren wants a direct report on the patrol information. You must bring what you learned back to Doren.

quest:335.text: A Noble Brew. Zardeth of the Black Claw schemes against Stormwind's nobles from beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. Lord Wishock's call for an investigation puts the hidden warlock coven at risk. Beneath the Mage Quarter streets, warlocks gather in the Slaughtered Lamb and keep their coven hidden. Lord Wishock, a member of the House of Nobles, has heard of the dark magic below the city. He is urging his peers to launch a full investigation, which could bring the city guard and royal scrutiny down on the coven.

quest:336.text: A Noble Brew. In Stormwind, a courier carries Black Claw Stout to Lord Baurles K. Wishock in the Royal Keep. Zardeth of the Black Claw has arranged the delivery from the cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb. Lord Baurles K. Wishock spends time in the Hall of Petitioners in Stormwind Keep, speaking of his own importance and the kingdom’s future. Patrons of the Slaughtered Lamb know another side of him. At night, he drinks in the tavern’s upper rooms and leaves large bills unpaid. By day, he petitions to have the tavern shut down.

quest:3369.text: In Nightmares. A shard from the Wailing Caverns brings a troubling vision to Thunder Bluff. Recovered as a glowing fragment, the Nightmare Shard is carried to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem on Elder Rise, where it reveals corruption within the Emerald Dream. Falla Sagewind sees the pure essence of the Emerald Dream in the strange crystal from the Wailing Caverns. A dark, chaotic vision dwells inside it, more waking nightmare than peaceful slumber. Unwilling to speak openly of such an omen, she entrusts the shard to you. She sends you to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, Thunder Bluff's most venerated elder druid.

quest:337.text: An Old History Book. In Stormwind, a lost chronicle returns to the Royal Library. Titled The History of Stormwind, the battered book bears the library’s seal and vanished before the kingdom was rebuilt after the First War. Its return gives Head Librarian Milton Sheaf a chance to preserve the history of southern human lands. Duskwood’s undead and ogres roam among the ruins where this mud-caked volume was found. The book is a rare relic from before Stormwind’s destruction. Its opening page bears the kingdom’s formal library seal. Someone checked it out decades ago, before the Horde razed the capital, and the book was presumed lost in the fall of the south. Milton Sheaf recognizes the book when it reaches him in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep. The head librarian means to place it in the rare books archive, though years in the haunted wilderness have badly damaged its pages. The discovery spurs Sheaf to seek more lost knowledge. He looks north to Southshore, the town nearest the ruined kingdom of Alterac and its abandoned libraries.

quest:3370.text: In Nightmares. Falla Sagewind sends a glowing shard to the elder druids in Darnassus. Its core holds the essence of the Emerald Dream, clouded by dark visions. Falla Sagewind finds more than a simple crystal in the glowing shard recovered from the depths of Wailing Caverns. She recognizes the pure essence of the Emerald Dream within it, yet the shard shows fearful visions instead of the harmony of nature. Shaken by what she sees, Falla refuses to study it further. She sends you to carry the shard to the senior druids of the Cenarion Circle.

quest:34.text: An Unwelcome Guest. An Unwelcome Guest is a local task in Lakeshire where resident Martie Jainrose seeks retribution against Bellygrub, a destructive wild boar. The beast has rampaged through her garden and trampled her seasonal daffodils, prompting a bounty on the creature's tusk. In the lakeside town of Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose tends to her domestic grounds amidst the gathering shadows over the Redridge Mountains. Her quiet routine is shattered by a persistent local terror: a notoriously aggressive wild boar that has repeatedly invaded her garden. Having trampled her prized patch of daffodils beyond recovery for the season, the distraught resident turns to capable travelers to put an end to the rampaging animal. The beast responsible is known to the locals as Bellygrub, an apt title coined by Lakeshire's town guard leader, Marshal Marris. Bellygrub spends the bulk of his time rooting and foraging through the brush in the fields southwest of the town. However, his voracious appetite and boldness often draw him dangerously close to civilized homes, culminating in the complete ruin of Martie's floral beds and demanding his definitive removal.

quest:343.text: Speaking of Fortitude. Brother Kristoff prepares a sermon in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light. For his message on the Fortitude of the Spirit, he seeks a book in Stormwind Keep's Royal Library. Brother Kristoff, a priest in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, is preparing a sermon on the Fortitude of the Spirit. He wants to draw on the craft of metalworking alongside scripture. To make his point, he needs a treatise called "The Stresses of Iron." Its lessons on bearing pressure may help his congregation understand the strength of faith. The Royal Library holds Stormwind's histories, civic writings, and other works within Stormwind Keep. Its shelves contain centuries of writing, so Brother Kristoff sends messengers to Head Librarian Milton Sheaf. Sheaf knows the archive by heart and can guide them to obscure works on crafts.

quest:344.text: Brother Paxton. At Stormwind's royal archives, Milton Sheaf sends you to Northshire Abbey for a missing dwarven treatise. The book was loaned months ago for copying, but has not returned to the city shelves. Stormwind's head librarian, Milton Sheaf, has a missing book on his hands. 'The Stresses of Iron,' a treatise on metallurgical techniques by dwarven prospector Margulf Blaggon, is gone from the capital's shelves. The book was loaned months ago to the clerics of Northshire Abbey so they could copy it. It was not misplaced in Stormwind. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton cares for the library and its books. The Holy Order of Northshire Clerics values knowledge, but copying a long technical manuscript by hand takes time. Paxton admits he has not finished duplicating Blaggon's work, so the original has yet to return to Stormwind.

quest:345.text: Ink Supplies. In Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton needs fresh ink for his work as a monastic scribe. He sends you east to Lakeshire for Rethban ore, the mineral his fast-drying ink requires. Brother Paxton takes pride in his craft and uses a special ink for important writings such as The Stresses of Iron. His recipe dries quickly and resists smearing, but the ink can dry in its pot if left too long. To make more, he needs raw Rethban iron ore, mined in the rocky Redridge Mountains. Lakeshire has little room for a distant scribe’s request. Foreman Oslow oversees laborers busy strengthening barricades, rebuilding ruined structures, and defending the town from ongoing Blackrock orc raids. With no workers to spare for mining, travelers must seek the ore in the perilous Rethban Caverns themselves.

quest:346.text: Return to Kristoff. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Stormwind for a borrowed book to return. After a long search and a delay in Northshire, you bring The Stresses of Iron back to the Cathedral of Light. Brother Kristoff is waiting in Cathedral Square for The Stresses of Iron, a book on metallurgy. Its trail led from Stormwind Keep's Royal Library to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton was copying the text by hand. Paxton ran short of Rethban ore for the scribe's ink, so the work stalled. With the ore retrieved and the copy complete, you bring the original book back to Stormwind. Northshire's copyists preserve civic and spiritual lore through patient work. Brother Paxton asks you to apologize to Librarian Milton Sheaf, a sign of how thin the abbey's resources have worn. Scribes must copy valuable books stroke by stroke with mineral-rich ink before returning them to Stormwind's care, making a book request a long undertaking.

quest:347.text: Rethban Ore. Foreman Oslow sends you into Rethban Caverns in Redridge for a dark mineral the scribes of Northshire Abbey need for ink. It is too soft for strong weapons or armor, but its color makes it useful for their work. Scribes at Northshire Abbey prize Rethban Ore for its dark, flat color. Bart Rethban discovered the mineral, but it has little use at an armorer’s anvil. Smelted metal from the ore lacks the strength needed for sturdy weapons or plate. Its raw color instead makes a valued base for manuscript dyes. The main deposits lie in the northern mountains of Redridge, inside Rethban Caverns. Lakeshire’s stoneworkers have left the cavern, driven out by a fierce band of Redridge gnolls. The gnolls put drudgers to work chipping ore from the rocky veins for their own crude purposes. Brother Paxton, a monk at Northshire Abbey, needs the pigment to copy historic texts. His work on The Stresses of Iron has stopped without the proper dye. Messengers and adventurers now travel into gnoll-held territory to bring him the raw stone.

quest:349.text: Stranglethorn Fever. Deep within Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa claims to know how to draw out the beast known as Mokk the Savage. Before communion with the spirits can begin, the witch doctor requires a Gorilla Fang as an offering. Once the ritual commences, defending the troll from agitated jungle beasts is necessary to lure the creature forth. Witch Doctor Unbagwa possesses the ritual knowledge needed to summon Mokk the Savage out of the surrounding jungle. To begin the incantation, the witch doctor demands a Gorilla Fang. Communing with the spirits carries a heavy risk, as the ritual chant draws the attention of other gorilla beasts in the vicinity, demanding protection while the magic does its work.

quest:350.text: Look to an Old Friend. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to seek an unusual contact in Stormwind's Trade District. Noble corruption shields traitors from ordinary justice, so Shaw turns to the city's finest cheesemonger and his intelligence network.

quest:3513.text: The Runed Scroll. A silvery ribbon marks the Runed Scroll found in Kalimdor's wilds as a formal message from across the border. Finding it sends Horde scouts to the Mor'shan Rampart to warn its guards of activity to the north. A fine silvery ribbon binds the scroll, unlike the rough leathers and parchment common in the Barrens. Its craft and script point to the night elves beneath Ashenvale's canopies to the north. With every ridge and road contested, a message taken from the enemy could matter greatly to the Horde's front lines. The scroll belongs with local command, not at the Warchief's hall in Orgrimmar. Kadrak, an orc warrior, watches the border from the Mor'shan Rampart, where the Barrens' red earth meets Ashenvale's forests. Bringing the scroll to this outpost gives its guards word of night elf troop movements.

quest:3514.text: Horde Presence. At the Barrens border, Kadrak sends a Horde champion into Stonetalon Peak after a missive is intercepted. The champion is to kill the dryad Rynthariel and plant a Horde banner inside the Talon Den. Kadrak watches the Barrens' northern boundary for Alliance and night elf incursions. After a messenger carrying a runed scroll is cut down, he decodes the missive and traces it to Rynthariel the Keymaster, an influential dryad in Stonetalon Peak. Kadrak chooses to strike rather than simply guard the mountain passes, hoping to deter future scouts from probing Horde territory. Horde warriors enter the Talon Den, a cavern overlooking Stonetalon Peak. Killing Rynthariel deals a blow to local night elf coordination. Kadrak's banner is planted inside the cave, its red standard marking the heart of dryad territory with a warning: incursions into the Barrens will meet decisive violence.

quest:359.text: Forsaken Duties. Forsaken Duties is a reconnaissance mission assigned by Magistrate Sevren in Brill to assess Scourge activity along the eastern perimeter of Tirisfal Glades. It establishes the constant threat posed by the Scourge slipping past The Bulwark and endangering local settlements. Magistrate Sevren oversees the security of Brill and the surrounding countryside, keeping a nervous eye on the eastern borders of Tirisfal Glades. With the Scourge swarming across the Western Plaguelands, Sevren requires constant reconnaissance from frontline sentries to ensure undead horrors do not slip past the perimeter unnoticed. Travelers willing to assist are dispatched south and east down the main thoroughfare to gather an urgent tactical assessment from Deathguard Linnea. Stationed at an eastern outpost along the road, Deathguard Linnea observes the frontier firsthand. Her findings confirm the magistrates fears: while the fortified position at The Bulwark successfully holds off the main Scourge host, small groups of undead manage to bypass the defenses on occasion. These stray forces have begun congregating around the nearby Balnir Farmstead, posing a localized but dangerous threat to Tirisfal Glades.

quest:373.text: The Unsent Letter. In the Deadmines, The Unsent Letter waits to be carried to Stormwind. Its delivery reveals the grievances and shared history binding Edwin VanCleef to the city's master builders. Edwin VanCleef falls aboard his juggernaut beneath Moonbrook, leaving behind more than a broken rebellion. A newly penned, sealed letter is tucked into his clothing. He addressed it not to a criminal lieutenant or financier, but to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect.

quest:3765.text: The Corruption Abroad. Argos Nightwhisper, a night elf envoy visiting Stormwind, seeks capable adventurers to cross the Great Sea and aid his brother in northern Kalimdor. His brother Gershala studies spreading ecological decay in Darkshore, where fresh hands are desperately needed. While Stormwind contends with internal turmoil and regional unrest, representatives from the distant kaldorei lands can be found wandering its stone streets. Argos Nightwhisper came seeking seasoned champions willing to look beyond human borders. The kaldorei are relatively new allies to the Eastern Kingdoms, and formal military aid is scarce, leaving family members and researchers to recruit whatever independent champions answer the call. The destination Argos points toward is Auberdine, a misty port town resting on the fog-shrouded coast of Darkshore. There, his brother Gershala conducts vital research into an ominous malaise afflicting the local wildlife and flora. Answering the summons means a long voyage from Stormwind Harbor across the Great Sea, marking a traveler's first real foray into the ancient wilderness of Kalimdor.

quest:377.text: Crime and Punishment. Crime and Punishment is an Alliance bounty originating in Darkshire that demands the extrajudicial execution of a grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Councilman Millstipe issues the contract after the House of Nobles overrides Duskwood's death sentence for Dextren Ward. Carrying out the hit satisfies local vengeance while delivering a sharp warning to the capital's negligent aristocracy. Duskwood already suffers beneath a shroud of creeping horrors and official indifference from the capital. When Dextren Ward was caught digging up fresh corpses from the Darkshire cemetery to sell to the necromancer Morbent Fel, the town's ruling council showed no mercy. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced the grave robber to beheadment. However, before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles intervened, claiming Ward as an imperial prisoner and transferring him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade. To Councilman Millstipe and the grieving citizens of Darkshire, sparing Ward from the headsman's block was an intolerable insult. The nobles in their secure city showed complete disregard for the torment suffered by frontier families whose dead relatives were fed into Fel's dark craft. Frustrated by Stormwind's bureaucratic meddling, Millstipe recruits daring mercenaries to infiltrate the riotous Stockade, assassinate Ward in his cell, and sever his hand as proof of execution.

quest:378.text: The Fury Runs Deep. Motley Garmason seeks vengeance against Kam Deepfury, now held in Stormwind's Stockade. Deepfury planned the assault on the Thandol Span, where Bronzebeard defenders died, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Stormwind keeps Deepfury as a political prisoner, so Motley turns to an adventurer to carry out dwarven justice. Clashes between Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and Dark Iron insurgents keep the northern Wetlands in turmoil. When the Thandol Span came under attack, sabotage took the lives of several dwarves, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Roggo gathered intelligence showing that Kam Deepfury planned the strike. Rather than face execution on the front lines, Deepfury was taken to the Stormwind Stockade as a political prisoner, not executed for murder. Motley Garmason is stationed at Dun Modr and refuses to let Stormwind's political calculations shield a war criminal. To him, human law puts decorum before blood debts. Bound to remain beside Longbraid in the Wetlands, Motley sends trusted champions beneath the human capital, into the rioting Stockade, to take Deepfury's head and settle the clan's score.

quest:386.text: What Comes Around.... Guard Berton in Lakeshire is pressing for Targorr the Dread's execution. The Blackrock orc remains in Stormwind Stockade despite his sentence, while political delays keep justice out of reach. Targorr the Dread earned his name in the Redridge Mountains, where he served as supreme executioner under General Gath'Ilzogg, chieftain of the Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep. Even among the invaders, his cruelty was notorious. He oversaw the torture and execution of many Redridge defenders. After his capture, Stormwind sent him to its high-security prison, the Stormwind Stockade, and condemned him to die for his crimes against the realm.

quest:387.text: Quell The Uprising. Warden Thelwater calls for help as the Stockade erupts in riot beneath Stormwind. Defias prisoners have seized the cell blocks, and he wants the uprising crushed before the city's leaders learn how badly the prison has failed. The Stockade holds criminals, conspirators, and outlaws who threaten the Kingdom of Stormwind. Imprisoned Defias operatives have launched a sudden, violent uprising and taken the cell blocks from the guards. Armed felons crowd the corridors, and the usual order has broken down. The guards now depend on visiting champions to fight through the riot and retake the prison. Warden Thelwater orders Defias prisoners killed on sight out of desperation and fear for his position. He suspects foul play behind the coordinated mutiny. If the House of Nobles or the wider nobility learns the Stockade is out of control, he fears he will lose his post. Thelwater hopes a death sentence for insurgency will break the inmates' resolve and crush the rebellion before word passes the canal gates.

quest:388.text: The Color of Blood. Nikova Raskol grieves for Mac, her young grandson, killed inside Stormwind City's prison. Anger consumes her, and she sends adventurers into The Stockade to take the Defias gang's red bandanas in retribution. Mac Raskol was fourteen when he took up arms as a guard in The Stockade. Stormwind's regular soldiers had been sent to distant fronts, leaving local defense to volunteers and the city's youth. Mac watched hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood in a place far more dangerous than his experience could prepare him for. The Defias inmates tore apart their wool prison blankets and made red bandanas from the scraps. The colors marked their loyalty to the Brotherhood, even behind prison walls. When Mac rebuked them and tried to enforce discipline, the prisoners stabbed him in the back. He died on the stone floor. Nikova Raskol turns from official channels to cold revenge after Mac's pointless death. She sends you into The Stockade to quell the rioting prisoners and bring back ten of their cherished red bandanas. Dyed the color of her grandson's spilled blood, the tokens offer a broken family a grim sense of closure.

quest:389.text: Bazil Thredd. In Stormwind, Bazil Thredd holds insight into the Defias Brotherhood's lingering plots. After an unsent letter is recovered from the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston directs you to the Defias leader's right-hand man, now locked beneath the streets in the high-security Stockade. Baros Alexston shares a bitter history with Edwin VanCleef. Both led the Stonemasons Guild, charged with rebuilding Stormwind from the ashes of the First and Second Wars. When the kingdom's magnificent white walls and towers were finished, the nobility refused to pay the masons their promised wages. Some senior members received bureaucratic posts to quiet them, but VanCleef refused to abandon the rank-and-file laborers. He led a violent riot out of the city and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:391.text: The Stockade Riots. At Stormwind's prison gates, Warden Thelwater sends you into the Stockade Riots to prove your loyalty to the city guards. The uprising has seized the prison, and he orders you to find and execute its ringleader, Bazil Thredd. Deep beneath the Mage Quarter's cobblestones, the Stockade has fallen into lawlessness. Criminals, Defias insurgents, and violent cutthroats have broken containment and seized the cell blocks, making the prison an impenetrable war zone. Warden Thelwater and his guards cling desperately to the entrance, unable to push inside and restore order by ordinary means.

quest:392.text: The Curious Visitor. After the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater has a troubling discovery about Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, a man named Maelik visited Thredd with legitimate papers. Warden Thelwater learned that Bazil Thredd had not been abandoned by his former comrades, as the guards believed. Months before the riot, a quiet visitor began meeting with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized paperwork, and gave his name as Maelik. Thelwater suspects the visits helped coordinate the bloody uprising. He gathers a physical description and sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston to learn who the visitor was.

quest:393.text: Shadow of the Past. In Stormwind, the trail from a Stockade prisoner leads into the city’s hidden dealings. Baros Alexston sends you to Mathias Shaw after a mysterious visitor spoke with Bazil Thredd. Baros Alexston cannot identify the visitor who spoke with Bazil Thredd, the Stockade’s chief prisoner. Warden Thelwater’s account has brought investigators to the city architect, but he has no name to offer. Instead, Baros points you toward Master Mathias Shaw, who leads SI:7 and makes it his business to know Stormwind’s secrets.

quest:394.text: The Head of the Beast. In Stormwind, The Head of the Beast carries you from Elling Trias to Master Mathias Shaw in Old Town. Reporting Lord Gregor Lescovar’s death confirms your place in Stormwind’s covert intelligence network. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind’s covert apparatus through SI:7 from hidden chambers in Old Town. When you report Lescovar’s death, Shaw recognizes your skill and ruthlessness, praises your efficiency, and thanks you for serving the people of Stormwind.

quest:395.text: Brotherhood's End. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Gregor Lescovar's killing leaves dangerous questions behind. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston and warns you to keep the killer's identity quiet. Baros Alexston, the City Architect who helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, is relieved to hear that Lescovar is dead. Edwin VanCleef had marked Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort for vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat to the kingdom's architects and nobility has passed.

quest:396.text: An Audience with the King. At Stormwind Keep, An Audience with the King brings the Defias report before the Crown. After the long investigation across Westfall and the Deadmines, the heroes carry City Architect Baros Alexston's findings to the capital. Edwin VanCleef has been defeated, and the conspiracy beneath Moonbrook has been dismantled. City Architect Baros Alexston prepares an official report for the Crown. He believes the adventurer who broke the guild's criminal enterprise should be honored before the monarch. You carry the detailed findings across Stormwind's grand canals to Stormwind Keep, expecting to meet the realm's sovereign.

quest:401.text: Wait for Sirra to Finish. In Darkshire's Town Hall, Sirra Von'Indi deciphers Abercrombie's cryptic note. As the resident scholar puts quill to paper, dread settles over the room, and the hermit's words hint at danger. Sirra Von'Indi has the note Abercrombie sent from his seclusion. The scholar aids the Night Watch and Darkshire's leaders, and needs only a short time to decipher the message. He does not yet know what horrors its words conceal.

quest:4021.text: Counterattack!. At Regthar Deathgate’s outpost west of the Crossroads, Kolkar warriors strike back after their leaders fall. They have crossed from Desolace, and Warlord Krom'zar leads their charge. The Kolkar have suffered a deep humiliation in the Barrens. Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark are dead, leaving the remaining centaur shattered and without direction. Word of their defeat travels west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. There, a fresh force of hardened Kolkar warriors rallies instead of scattering into the scrubland. Burning for blood and retribution, they cross into the Barrens and march against the young Horde encampments.

quest:442.text: Assault on Fenris Isle. Forsaken agents move against the Scourge on Fenris Isle. High Executor Hadrec sends them to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of Thule Ravenclaw, the necromancer commanding the island stronghold in Lake Lordamere. The Forsaken hold the western roads and have established their presence at the Sepulcher, but the Scourge remain entrenched in Fenris Keep. The island lies in Lake Lordamere, east of Silverpine Forest, and its forces threaten the forest and the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity. High Executor Hadrec sees Thule Ravenclaw’s vile experiments as a danger to Forsaken control of Silverpine. Thule commands the Scourge from the keep, keeping their power close to the Forsaken shore.

quest:4542.text: Message to Freewind Post. Message to Freewind Post is a Horde quest tasking travelers with carrying urgent dispatches from Brave Moonhorn near the border lifts down into Thousand Needles. The missive warns Cliffwatcher Longhorn of intensifying centaur raids against local caravans. It also raises early concerns regarding the suspicious, standoffish behavior of the neighboring Grimtotem clan. Standing watch near the canyon's western approaches, Brave Moonhorn keeps a vigil over the roads leading down into Thousand Needles. With centaur aggression abruptly spiking, communication between border sentries and the regional leadership is vital. Moonhorn entrusts passing Horde adventurers with carrying an urgent dispatch southeast to Cliffwatcher Longhorn, the commander stationed atop the mesa settlement of Freewind Post. Upon receiving the message, Longhorn confirms the dire situation: a recent supply caravan was intercepted and slaughtered by marauding centaur, leaving Freewind Post in desperate need of retaliation and defense. Just as concerning is Moonhorn's parting caution to avoid the local Grimtotem tauren, whose uncharacteristically bizarre and hostile demeanor hints at deeper rifts brewing across the arid flats.

quest:455.text: The Algaz Gauntlet. Orcs have seized Dun Algaz, the pass between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. The Dragonmaw threaten Ironforge's route to Menethil Harbor, and Mountaineer Rockgar sends Alliance travelers to strike them and carry word to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz cuts through the crags between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. It is the only overland mountain pass between them. Ironforge depends on it for trade, troop movements, and supplies bound for Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's main coastal port in the region. If the pass falls, Ironforge's route to the western seas is cut, and isolated outposts lose access to dwarven reinforcements. Dragonmaw remnants have haunted the hills and ruins of the Wetlands since the Second War, but now they have pushed into Dun Algaz in an organized assault. Their scouts and grunts have seized the tunnels and fortified the pass. Mountaineer Rockgar asks Alliance travelers to slay the orcs and carry word of the attack to Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor.

quest:4581.text: Kayneth Stillwind. Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire sends a courier east from Astranaar with a scouting missive for Forest Song. Druid Kayneth Stillwind needs help watching corruption spread through Ashenvale's ancient woods. In Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire watches over western Ashenvale. Druid Kayneth Stillwind, stationed at Forest Song in the forest's eastern reaches, has asked her to assess the region's security. Shifting wildlife and dark omens along the coasts and through the woods trouble him. Swiftfire puts her observations in a sealed note, trusting a traveler to carry it safely across the dangerous central forest. The way to Forest Song crosses Nightsong Woods, where satyrs encroach, wildlife turns hostile, and the Horde makes excursions from the south. At Forest Song's shrine, Kayneth Stillwind studies the balance of Ashenvale's natural spirits. Swiftfire's reconnaissance confirms his fear that corruption is spreading through the forest, not confined to one place or passing quickly. The druids will need more help to confront the wickedness taking root.

quest:463.text: The Greenwarden. First Mate Fitzsimmons sends Alliance travelers from Menethil Harbor northeast into the Wetlands marshes. They seek a mysterious being rumored to dwell among the beasts. Sailors and wanderers at Menethil Harbor trade stories of a beast lurking in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons describes the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs and calls those who seek it gullible. Leave the dry road, he warns, and “ol’ Greenie” will bite you in two. To the folk on the docks, anything huge in the murky waters is another man-eating danger in the marsh.

quest:464.text: War Banners. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist sends Alliance champions against Dragonmaw orcs gathering strength in the Wetlands. He wants their war banners claimed from a camp northeast of town. The Dragonmaw clan once held the red dragonflight captive at Grim Batol during the Second War. When that control broke, the freed dragons hunted their captors nearly to extinction. The few orcs who survived fled Grim Batol into the high mountains east of Whelgar's Excavation, hiding from the red flight's wrath. Dragonmaw survivors have gathered again northeast of Menethil Harbor. They have raised a war camp and planted crimson standards in the marsh. Captain Stoutfist sees danger in an armed orc force so near the harbor town. He wants their ranks cut down and their banners torn away as proof of defeat.

quest:465.text: Nek'rosh's Gambit. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist fears a Dragonmaw siege. Chieftain Nek'rosh has built engines to bombard the vulnerable port town, while fighting at Dun Algaz cuts off reinforcements. You are sent into the marshes to destroy the catapults before the attack begins. Dwarven scouts uncovered Nek'rosh's plan as Alliance fighters clashed with Dragonmaw raiders. The chieftain has overseen the building of full-scale siege catapults in the Wetlands encampments. He means to bring the engines to Menethil Harbor and batter its fortress walls, threatening the Alliance's main shipping hub on the western coast. Fighting and greenskin activity have congested the mountain passes at Dun Algaz, isolating the lowlands from Ironforge's main garrisons. Without aid from Khaz Modan, Captain Stoutfist cannot spare troops to guard the harbor's perimeter. Menethil's survival depends on sabotaging the catapults before they can be brought against the town. Scouts carry Dwarven Tinder into the heart of the Dragonmaw encampment. They must set the timber catapults ablaze and destroy them, stripping Nek'rosh of his artillery and denying his warriors the firepower to break Menethil's defenses. The engines must be ruined before the warlord himself can be confronted.

quest:466.text: Search for Incendicite. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear seeks samples of volatile incendicite ore from the Wetlands. He believes its explosive force could change dwarven artillery, and needs miners to reach a secluded cave and bring back the dangerous mineral. Incendicite, a rare and unstable mineral, has drawn the attention of siege engine pilots and mechanics at Steelgrill's Depot. Rich veins are rumored to lie in a cavern northwest of Algaz Gate, in the Wetlands. The ore is highly reactive and dangerous to handle. Careless miners have found it detonating in their faces. Pilot Stonegear sees military promise in the dangerous ore. Refined correctly, incendicite could power dwarven artillery or serve as its payload, giving cannon shells force enough to break fortified defenses. Stonegear wants raw samples so researchers can test ways to smelt it without blowing up the depot.

quest:467.text: Stonegear's Search. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear seeks a rare ore for his tank. He asks a daring traveler to find fresh fuel for its weapons. Pilot Stonegear, stationed just outside Ironforge, wants to make his siege engine more powerful. Word of his plans spreads through Ironforge and Loch Modan. Pilot Longbeard or Mountaineer Kadrell may send you to meet the ambitious pilot and hear his proposal. Pilot Stonegear works at Steelgrill's Depot, a proving ground and staging yard along the road just east of Kharanos. He seeks prospectors willing to search for a rare, volatile ore. He believes it can greatly increase his tank's firepower.

quest:468.text: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Mountaineer Kadrell sends you north from Loch Modan to join Rockgar at Dun Algaz. Rockgar is organizing an expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands, along the pass between the dwarven homeland and the northern territories. Dun Algaz cuts through the northern ridge, linking Loch Modan with the marshy Wetlands. The fortified pass carries trade, messengers, and military detachments between Ironforge and Alliance settlements farther north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell watches travelers on the road and recruits hardy volunteers for the northern outposts.

quest:469.text: Daily Delivery. Einar Stonegrip keeps to the Wetlands while his hides make their way to Menethil Harbor. He asks travelers bound for town to carry cured crocolisk hides to a local tanner. Einar Stonegrip hunts the wildlife of the Wetlands, especially the aggressive crocolisks along its waterways. He gathers plenty of valuable skins, but taking them home means traveling to Menethil Harbor. With his marriage to Sida going through a rough patch, Einar would rather remain in the field than face her. He hands his parcels to travelers passing toward town. James Halloran tans hides in Menethil Harbor. Local hunters supply him with leather for boots and goods that merchants and sailors passing through the port can use. Einar has been away for a week, and Halloran guesses a quarrel with Sida explains the delivery by proxy. He wonders if his own wife should step in and make peace with her.

quest:470.text: Digging Through the Ooze. In Menethil Harbor, Sida asks travelers to recover her bag from the ooze that swallowed it. She visits Ironbeard's Tomb regularly, but fled when foul oozes filled the barrows. Sida lives in Menethil Harbor and often travels northeast into the Wetlands to pay homage at Ironbeard's Tomb. On her latest visit, foul, dripping oozes had filled the ancient barrow. She panicked and hurled her satchel at one of them. The ooze swallowed the bag whole, giving Sida just enough time to flee back to the port town. Now she asks travelers to search for it. Ironbeard's Tomb lies near Dun Modr, the contested stronghold, and holds the remains of a storied dwarven hero. Corruption in the surrounding marshland draws amorphous, acidic slimes that consume anything in their path. Sida cannot remember which creature swallowed her belongings. Travelers must search the tomb grounds and cut through the creeping blight to find her drenched satchel.

quest:471.text: Apprentice's Duties. James Halloran needs giant crocolisk hides after his apprentice is mauled in the marshes. The tanner in Menethil Harbor asks travelers to finish the dangerous harvest. James Halloran sent his young apprentice into the Wetlands marshes to skin giant crocolisks. When the boy did not return, Halloran searched for him and found him badly mauled by the beasts. Menethil Harbor's tradesmen depend on materials from the surrounding country, where the bogs make such work dangerous. The town midwife believes Halloran's apprentice will survive, though the attack cost him a leg. Halloran needs hides for his trade and wants vengeance on the beasts that tore into the boy he loves like a son. He asks travelers to go north along the coast, past the murloc hovels, and hunt the giant crocolisks.

quest:472.text: Fall of Dun Modr. At Dun Modr, a northern fortress has fallen to a violent Dark Iron assault. In Menethil Harbor, a severely wounded survivor seeks an Alliance adventurer to go north and learn whether commander Longbraid the Grim or any of the garrison survived. For generations, Dun Modr has guarded northern Khaz Modan and the vital road and bridge across the Thandol Span, linking the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. After an ambush at the bridge, the garrison fell back to regroup inside the fortress. Before they could restore their defenses, overwhelming Dark Iron forces struck, slaughtering the defenders and driving them into a desperate flight. Harlo Barnaby, a young defender, was gravely wounded when a stray axe struck his back during the retreat. Believing him doomed, Longbraid the Grim and the remaining troops strapped Barnaby to their last surviving horse and sent him south to Menethil Harbor. He survived and awoke in the harbor tavern, burdened by survivor's guilt and entirely unaware whether any of his comrades had escaped alive.

quest:473.text: Report to Captain Stoutfist. After the fighting at Dun Algaz, Report to Captain Stoutfist sends proven fighters into Menethil Harbor's keep. The harbor is an Alliance military post, where Valstag Ironjaw directs you to Captain Stoutfist as the Dragonmaw threat spreads across the Wetlands. Dwarven mountaineers have watched the narrow passes of Dun Algaz for years. The Dragonmaw clan's return reaches beyond Loch Modan, though, as the orcs push outward, raise encampments, and threaten the marshlands. Valstag Ironjaw knows that holding the pass is only the first step in protecting the road to Ironforge. Captain Stoutfist oversees Menethil Harbor's defenses from the war room inside Menethil Keep. Dark Iron saboteurs, local beasts, and marsh murlocs all threaten the port, so the captain depends on capable volunteers to counter dangers beyond the walls. Valstag sends you to carry out direct orders against the Dragonmaw war machine.

quest:4736.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Across the sea, Alliance warlocks seek Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. From Strahad Farsan's tower above Ratchet, she teaches seasoned practitioners to craft tools and garments that strengthen their control of demons. Briarthorn sees when a warlock has moved beyond basic demonology and resisted corruption. He sends those pupils beyond Ironforge, across the sea to Kalimdor, instead of keeping them beneath the mountain. There, they can learn practical felcraft from an artisan with greater skill. Strahad Farsan keeps a solitary tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. Warlocks often set aside racial and political borders to survive in a world wary of dark magic. Menara Voidrender stays at Strahad's sanctuary and works with warlocks of every allegiance, helping them sharpen their craft and keep their summoned fiends bound.

quest:4737.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Zevrost sends warlocks from Orgrimmar to seek Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. He warns that fel magic leads to demonic enslavement, yet points them toward a mentor who can help fashion powerful arcane vestments. Warlocks gather beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, where their presence is tolerated uneasily. Zevrost, one of their bitter tutors, sneers at acolytes who seek mastery of the dark arts. He believes those who delve deeper into fel magic only hasten their own enslavement. In his view, demonic addiction will eventually overtake every practitioner, turning even the most disciplined scholar into a thrall of the Twisting Nether. Zevrost admits that other warlocks do not share his bleak view. Word has reached Orgrimmar of Menara Voidrender, a skilled warlock on the bluffs overlooking Ratchet, the neutral goblin port. Menara seeks promising disciples to help craft specialized implements for wielding their arcane might. For warlocks eager to advance their craft, her summons begins the forging of the legendary Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. Menara waits high above Ratchet, where the realities of warlock society are plain. Warlocks must set aside racial and cultural rivalries and support one another. The demons they bargain with show no prejudice and no mercy to anyone who falters. Sharing knowledge and crafting protective vestments comes from practical need, not noble charity: warlocks must survive the hostile entities they bind to their service.

quest:4738.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. An Alliance warlock seeking to craft powerful vestments is directed by the Mage Quarter's covert practitioners to seek out Menara Voidrender across the Great Sea. Stationed high above the neutral port of Ratchet, Menara trains dark spellcasters across faction divides in the dangerous arts of binding and artifact creation. Within the dark crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, warlock trainer Demisette Cloyce is known for her strict, unsparing standards. When an aspiring warlock reaches the threshold of weaving significant items of power, Demisette rarely believes they are truly ready. Nevertheless, higher authorities within the cabal mandate the student's advancement, dispatching them far from the safety of the capital to prove their mettle. The destination is the arid hills overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. There, Menara Voidrender maintains her laboratory in a stone tower. Isolated from the strict laws of Stormwind and the watchful eyes of Orgrimmar, Menara accepts apprentices regardless of race or political allegiance, knowing that the fiends and demonic entities warlocks contend with harbor equal malice toward every mortal soul.

quest:4739.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Menara Voidrender awaits Horde warlocks ready for deeper study in Ratchet. From the Undercity, they cross the Great Sea to her hilltop refuge above the port. Kaal Soulreaper watches warlocks grow more skilled in the Undercity. When one outgrows simple hexes and impish thralls, he sends them across the Great Sea for specialized instruction. Demonic control leaves little room for error. A skilled mentor can help a warlock survive the volatile powers of the Nether. Strahad Farsan’s tower rises from a high bluff above Ratchet. Away from the scrutiny of city guards, practitioners such as Menara Voidrender teach younger initiates. Warlocks from different backgrounds set aside tribal and political rivalries. The demons they bargain with will consume human, orc, or Forsaken alike if their summoner’s will falters.

quest:474.text: Defeat Nek'rosh. In the Wetlands, the Alliance campaign against the Dragonmaw reaches its final strike. With their siege engines sabotaged, the defenders turn on Chieftain Nek'rosh to secure Menethil Harbor. His severed head must be brought to Captain Stoutfist to break the threat to the coastal port. The Dragonmaw have long plagued the marshlands of Khaz Modan, entrenched in fortified camps and threatening Menethil Harbor's sea lanes. After discovering and burning the clan's catapults, the marsh's defenders strike at the warband's leader. Chieftain Nek'rosh commands the local orcs and remains the last obstacle to breaking the siege. His death leaves the remaining raiders without their leader's direction. Bring Nek'rosh's severed head to Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor, and Ironforge's garrison will claim a major victory. Without their heavy siege weapons or their chieftain, the Dragonmaw suffer a blow they are unlikely to recover from quickly. Menethil Harbor is the Alliance's main lifeline between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan. With Nek'rosh fallen, the port's docks and trade vessels are safer from sudden attack.

quest:4767.text: Wind Rider. Wind Rider is a Horde quest offered by Elu atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Aspiring to become a wind rider himself, Elu tasks adventurers with climbing into the craggy heights of Highperch to gather wild wyvern eggs to bolster the Horde's aerial mount reserves. Across Kalimdor, the Horde relies heavily on wind riders to ferry couriers, scouts, and warriors across vast distances. At Freewind Post, a young tauren named Elu aspires to join their esteemed ranks. With the demands of the expanding Horde outpacing the availability of mounts, Elu has been charged with helping procure new wyverns to supply the master wind riders, offering eager travelers a chance to assist in this vital effort. Highperch rises atop the towering mesas of Thousand Needles, serving as a prime nesting ground for wild wyverns. Gathering viable eggs requires braving the cliffs and facing the fiercely protective adults that patrol the roosts. By securing these clutches, Elu hopes to prove his dedication and begin the rigorous process of hand-raising and training wyverns for the Horde's flight masters.

quest:4770.text: Homeward Bound. Homeward Bound is a Horde quest that tasks adventurers with rescuing Pao'ka Swiftmountain, a young tauren naturalist stranded in the wyvern nesting grounds of Highperch. After getting separated and lost while studying the dangerous beasts, Pao'ka must be escorted safely down the cliffs back toward Whitereach Post. Pao'ka Swiftmountain accompanied the elder Motega Firemane to Thousand Needles to study the unique wildlife of the canyon floor and its towering stone pillars. Driven by curiosity and overconfidence, Pao'ka crept alone into the heights of Highperch to observe the local wyverns firsthand. The territorial beasts drove him off, leaving the young scholar stranded, terrified, and hiding among the crags for days. Highperch is thick with aggressive wyverns fiercely guarding their clutches and high roosts. Escorting Pao'ka back to level ground requires carving a path straight through the nesting predators. Unprepared for open combat, the panicked youth relies entirely on passing Horde travelers to fend off the swarming wyverns until he reaches the relative safety of the canyon path leading east.

quest:480.text: The Weaver. In Silverpine Forest, Ataeric works to awaken a dormant ley energy node for Dalaran. Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher sends you to stop the archmage and take his staff, keeping Dalaran’s magic from threatening Forsaken control of the southern reaches of Lordaeron. After earlier inquiries into Ambermill and Dalaran’s movements, the Forsaken learned that the wizards are trying to awaken a dormant ley energy node in Silverpine Forest. If Dalaran gains its concentrated arcane power, it could strengthen its position and threaten the Undercity’s hold over southern Lordaeron.

quest:4821.text: Alien Egg. Rumors among the tauren of Freewind Post speak of a bizarre, foreign egg guarded fiercely by wild serpents on the canyon floor. Hagar Lightninghoof tasks Horde adventurers with tracking down and retrieving the specimen before whatever lurks inside breaks free. Word reached Freewind Post of an unusual egg spotted deep in the serpent dens that dot the canyon floor beneath the towering stone needles. The serpents native to the canyon watch over the egg as though it were their own brood, striking out at any traveler who ventures too close. Intrigued and wary of what might threaten the local hunting grounds, Hagar Lightninghoof asks brave scouts to locate the clutch, bypass the slithering sentries, and secure the oddity for study.

quest:484.text: Young Crocolisk Skins. In Menethil Harbor, prominent tanner James Halloran needs fresh skins from young marsh crocolisks. Their cured hides are in demand across the sea, so steady hunting keeps his trade supplied. Bringing him the softer skins earns his trust and leads to more leatherworking chores. Menethil Harbor links the Eastern Kingdoms to distant continents, and its busy local economy draws on the surrounding marsh. James Halloran tans and cures hides from the region's abundant reptilian predators for trade across the sea. Merchants and ships carry his leather goods to distant ports, keeping pressure on his workshop to maintain a steady supply. Einar brings Halloran regular hauls of mature hides, but those are too firm for some luxury goods. Halloran relies on passing travelers to fill the shortage of softer leather by hunting young crocolisks in the shallow bogs just outside Menethil's palisades. The skins must stay intact for Halloran's careful curing process.

quest:4841.text: Pacify The Centaur. Pacify the Centaur is a retaliatory hunting mission issued by Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post. Charged with clearing the threat gathering beneath the canyon spires, Horde adventurers strike deep into the Galak centaur encampments of Splithoof Crag. Perched upon its precarious desert mesa, Freewind Post grants the tauren a commanding vantage over the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. However, that high ground offers little peace when hostile enemies mass directly beneath the ropes and elevators. The Galak centaur have established a sprawling war camp nestled directly north along the canyon wall at Splithoof Crag, directly menacing supply lines and tauren movement through the needles. To counter the growing danger, Cliffwatcher Longhorn sends capable Horde travelers to thin the Galak ranks through unsparing violence. Rather than merely defending the access lifts, the tauren believe the only way to safeguard Freewind Post is to break the centaur vanguard in their own camp. Taking down their scouts, beast-wranglers, and windchaser mystics is meant to blunt any concerted assault on the post before it can begin.

quest:4865.text: Serpent Wild. Serpent Wild is a Horde quest in Thousand Needles that connects the discovery of strange alien eggs to ancient tauren legends. Following an unsettling revelation at Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof dispatches adventurers northwest to Motega Firemane at Whitereach Post to confront the awakening of Arikara. When strange, unnatural eggs began appearing in Thousand Needles, local tauren feared an ecological disaster. However, inspecting the artifacts reveals something far older and more ominous than ordinary predators: signs pointing to the vengeance spirit Arikara. Stunned by the horrifying confirmation, Hagar Lightninghoof realizes the canyon faces a mythical threat long thought relegated to fireside lore. Recognizing that the threat surpasses simple physical defense, Hagar urges immediate council with Motega Firemane. Stationed northwest along the canyon floor at Whitereach Post, Motega serves as a watcher and spiritual guide versed in the traditional omens of the Needles. His guidance is essential if the Horde hopes to understand and appease or destroy the rising vengeance spirit.

quest:4881.text: Assassination Plot. Assassination Plot is a Horde quest initiated by recovering intercepted centaur orders in Thousand Needles. The orders reveal an impending strike targeting the tauren Kanati Greycloud at his hunting camp by Whitereach Post. Thousand Needles has long been contested terrain dominated by warring centaur clans and dangerous wildlife. When the tauren brave Kanati Greycloud set up a hunting camp at Whitereach Post, the small post southwest of the Great Lift, the local centaur viewed it as an audacious intrusion into their territory. Rather than merely driving game away, the centaur resolved to eliminate Greycloud entirely to discourage any further Horde expansion through the canyon.

quest:490.text: Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg is an Alliance quest authorized by the Sentinels to curb the aggressive furbolg population corrupting Teldrassil. Shayla Nightbreeze recruits adventurers outside Darnassus to hunt the corrupted beasts and collect their fangs as proof of deed. On the road outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze acts on direct orders from the Sentinels to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. Once peaceful inhabitants of the ancient forests, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading corruption that stripped away their reason, turning them into vicious threats to the safety of travelers and the natural sanctity of Teldrassil. To curb the Gnarlpine aggression, hunters are dispatched across the boughs of the World Tree to cull their ranks and collect their fangs as proof. The bulk of their corrupted population resides in two major strongholds: Ban'ethil Hollow, set south of the road west of Dolanaar, and the ruins of Starbreeze Village toward the east.

quest:4904.text: Free At Last. Free at Last is a rescue mission atop the windswept spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Lakota Windsong, a tauren woman held captive by Arnak Grimtotem, needs protection as she flees her captor's stronghold and returns to her friend Thalia Amberhide at Freewind Post. The Grimtotem clan's aggressive presence in Thousand Needles is not limited to skirmishes over land. Arnak Grimtotem sought to take Lakota Windsong as his bride, but when she refused his advances, he chose violence. Arnak returned in the night, struck down Lakota's brother when he tried to defend her, and dragged her away to Darkcloud Pinnacle. Perched across the high wooden suspension bridges above Thousand Needles, Darkcloud Pinnacle is swarming with hostile Grimtotem warriors. Escorting Lakota requires navigating the descent while fighting off waves of Grimtotem bandits intent on recapturing her before she reaches the canyon floor. Once safely down from the pinnacle, Lakota makes her way back to the safety of Freewind Post. Her companion, Thalia Amberhide, receives the news with immense relief but deep mourning for Lakota's fallen brother, offering his remaining belongings as a token of gratitude to those who brought her home alive.

quest:493.text: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Renferrel sends his research south to Tarren Mill, where the Forsaken press on with their plague studies. You carry his notes from Silverpine Forest to Apothecary Lydon in Hillsbrad Foothills. Since escaping the Lich King's control, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has pursued a New Plague that could destroy both the living and the Scourge. The Royal Apothecary Society works under the Banshee Queen's relentless pressure to create it. Its researchers are scattered across Lordaeron, so they share chemical data and test findings to hasten their work. Apothecary Renferrel works from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest and sends you south with his recent findings for Apothecary Lydon. Your road leaves the pine woods and crosses the open pastures of Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill lies beneath the Alterac Mountains, serving the Forsaken as an outpost and a place to stage their research.

quest:494.text: Time to Strike. At the Hillsbrad border, Time to Strike carries Lesh's signal east to Tarren Mill. Her coded message moves word from a quiet watch to Forsaken plans against Hillsbrad's humans. Deathstalker Lesh watches the valley from high ground near the border of Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills. Below, human settlers and militia move through the valley. The Deathstalkers serve as the Undercity's eyes and ears, watching enemy settlements before troops deploy. Lesh stays at her post and asks passing Horde travelers to carry her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

quest:496.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon pursues lethal brews against the living. He turns to travelers for animal reagents from the surrounding foothills. Tarren Mill is both a Forsaken stronghold in the Hillsbrad Foothills and a research station for the Royal Apothecary Society. Apothecary Lydon works there amid the green countryside, which he despises. He longs to see human settlements poisoned and conquered. To make his experimental Elixir of Suffering, he needs potent, virulent ingredients from nearby creatures. Apothecary Lydon sends hunters into the wilds around Tarren Mill for Gray Bear tongues and the rare ichor of Moss Creepers. Unholy alchemy refines these animal substances into the basis of a lethal mixture. He intends it to kill living trespassers across Hillsbrad.

quest:4966.text: Protect Kanati Greycloud. Protect Kanati Greycloud is a Horde quest at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Warned that centaur assassins have targeted the tauren Kanati Greycloud, adventurers must make a stand beside him and repel a squad of Galak assassins. While stationed among the towering sandstone spires of Whitereach Post, the tauren Kanati Greycloud learns from intercepted centaur orders of an assassination plot directed squarely at his life. The Galak tribe of centaur, relentless in their hostility toward the nomadic tauren and their Horde allies, are not content merely raiding supply paths; they seek to eliminate those who settle in their canyons. Realizing the attack is imminent and suspecting the enemy forces might outnumber his initial estimates, Kanati asks travelers at the post to fight alongside him. When the Galak assassins strike, Kanati stands his ground, relying on allied blades and spells to break the ambush before the centaur can claim their prize.

quest:498.text: The Rescue. In Tarren Mill, Krusk seeks help after Syndicate bandits capture the orc scouts sent into Durnholde Keep. Thrall had sent the party to investigate the growing threat and retrieve an object from the keep. Warchief Thrall sent a band of orc warriors to the Hillsbrad Foothills to investigate the growing Syndicate threat and retrieve an object from Durnholde Keep. Gol'dir led the scouts toward the fortress ruins, where the Syndicate's numbers overwhelmed them in an ambush. Krusk broke free and limped back across the river to Tarren Mill. Drull, Tog'thar, and Gol'dir were captured by the human bandits.

quest:499.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon prepares a poison for the Royal Apothecary Society. He wants to know how swiftly it kills before using it more widely. Apothecary Lydon works in Tarren Mill to make chemical weapons for the Dark Lady's ambitions. His blight is meant to destroy both the living humans of the Alliance and the undead horrors of the Scourge. Once he has the needed reagents, Lydon mixes them into a foul brew he calls the Elixir of Suffering. He is eager to see its power before the Society uses it on a wider scale.

quest:5.text: Jitters' Growling Gut. In Raven Hill, Jitters is starving and afraid, with only weeds and insects to eat. He asks you to go east to Darkshire and seek a hot batch of Chef Grual’s famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill’s ruined streets shelter ravenous undead and lurking beasts. Jitters has hidden there for weeks, moving through its crumbling shanties under a sky that never seems to brighten. Grubs from the dirt and wild weeds are all he has found to eat. Hunger and fear wear him down, far from the comforts of ordinary life. Jitters longs for a taste of safety: the seasoned patties made at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He asks you to cross the haunted road and speak with Chef Grual. If the chef agrees to make Dusky Crab Cakes, a hot meal may quiet Jitters’ growling gut.

quest:501.text: Elixir of Pain. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon seeks mountain lion blood for a lethal brew. His work serves the Royal Apothecary Society’s drive to perfect the New Plague. Apothecary Lydon finds little joy in Tarren Mill’s surroundings. From his window, the blooming meadows and brisk mountain air of Hillsbrad seem an offense to him. Like many in the Royal Apothecary Society, Lydon devotes himself to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the New Plague. The Society seeks to perfect this engineered scourge, meant to kill the living and bring retribution to its enemies. Lydon seeks ingredients for his latest poisonous mixture among the animals prowling the foothills and the slopes toward the Alterac Mountains. He believes mountain lion blood has properties needed to make what he calls an Elixir of Pain. So he sends agents into the wilds to collect ten vials. The blood will support the Society’s continuing chemical trials along the contested southern front.

quest:502.text: Elixir of Pain. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon prepares the Elixir of Pain for a field trial. Stanley, Farmer Ray’s dog in Hillsbrad Fields, is the chosen subject. Apothecary Lydon works in Tarren Mill for the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. He gathers fresh blood from local wildlife and uses it to brew a volatile mixture called the Elixir of Pain. The Society seeks field evidence of how its experimental poisons and mutagens affect living bodies. Lydon sends his agents to the northern farm in Hillsbrad Fields, away from the human defenders. Farmer Ray keeps a pet dog there named Stanley. With the draught poured into an open hand, an agent offers it to the unsuspecting dog as an ordinary treat.

quest:503.text: Gol'dir. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has found where Gol'dir is held. The documents point to a large Syndicate base up north, possibly in the Alterac Mountains, and Gol'dir has been captive too long. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has studied the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to a large Syndicate base up north, possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has been held too long, and Krusk wants him freed. Gol'dir is held in the top room of the inn at Strahnbrad, where Syndicate fill the building. A Rusted Iron Key opens the lock. Jailor Borhuin carries it and may be in any building in town.

quest:5042.text: Agamaggan's Strength. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers Agamaggan's Strength in return for Blood Shards. The captive Razormane shaman draws on his people's reverence for the ancient boar demigod and his hatred of the rival Bristleback tribe. The quilboar honor Agamaggan, an ancient boar demigod whose spilled blood is said to have formed the red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. They treat the crystals as sacred, drawing on their power to strengthen their front-line fighters. Mangletooth, an elder Razormane shaman held captive in Camp Taurajo, offers this strength to Horde champions. He claims your foes will cower as they do before the Razormane's mightiest champions. Mangletooth offers his strength out of spite. The orcs and tauren captured and caged the old quilboar, whose Razormane tribe is at war with the rival Bristleback. Unable to break his chains and slaughter them himself, he trades Agamaggan's gifts for help against them. He rewards those who destroy Bristleback tribes and take the sacred Blood Shards from their lands.

quest:5043.text: Agamaggan's Agility. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a blood shard ritual. The captive quilboar channels the power of his ancient boar god, blessing those who bring him shards from the Barrens with swift movement and sure aim. Crimson blood shards jut from the Barrens soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition says the crystals formed from Agamaggan's spilled blood. The Great Boar Ancient fell fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked in a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth knows how to channel the stones' dormant divine power for anyone who brings them. Quilboar hunters and scouts prize ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. For four blood shards, Mangletooth calls on the fallen demi-god's latent energy, lending the petitioner the instincts and supple grace of his people's best stalkers. He grunts with disdain at outsiders, yet honors his pact and weaves Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

quest:5044.text: Wisdom of Agamaggan. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth trades the wisdom of Agamaggan for blood shards. The captive quilboar offers Horde spellcasters a ritual drawn from the ancient boar god’s power. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth is held prisoner by the Horde. The quilboar trades his people’s magical secrets for blood shards, crimson crystals said to have formed from Agamaggan’s spilled blood. The towering boar Demigod died in the War of the Ancients.
