Mangletooth says the geomancers and shaman of his tribes use the shards to channel divine power in their rituals. Other shard offerings bring physical resilience or swiftness. Mangletooth’s Wisdom ritual instead sharpens intellect and arcane ability. For four blood shards, he calls on Agamaggan’s spirit to grant you cunning in your confrontations, then reminds you of your mortality.

quest:5045.text: Rising Spirit. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a ritual blessing drawn from Agamaggan's ancient power. Bring blood shards taken from his Bristleback rivals, and he strengthens your will and spirit. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth knows the geomancy and ancestral magic of the quilboar. He takes pride in his people's devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. To Mangletooth, an unbroken spirit carries a warrior onward when strength fails and defeat seems near. Mangletooth asks for blood shards to raise your spirit. These crystals hold Agamaggan's ancient blood, which seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. Bring him shards gathered across the Barrens, especially from his Bristleback enemies, and he can channel their power into a blessing that bolsters your will.

quest:5046.text: Razorhide. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Razorhide to those who bring him blood shards. The captive quilboar trades Agamaggan’s life essence for a blessing that hardens the skin before battle. The quilboar trace their power to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who died fighting the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood sank into the Barrens and hardened into crystalline shards, still alive with ancient power. The Horde and quilboar remain sworn enemies, yet Mangletooth, held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, will share sacred knowledge for these fragments. Quilboar are born with thick hides and protective quills, but their warriors call on Agamaggan to harden their skin against blades and claws. Mangletooth can perform the rite for outsiders, channeling four blood shards to strengthen their defenses and help keep their bones unbroken in the wilds.

quest:5052.text: Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Across the Barrens, blood shards carry the power of the fallen boar god Agamaggan. Quilboar say his blood sank into the earth and hardened into red stones. At Camp Taurajo, the captive Mangletooth trades their power to the Horde for his own reasons. Quilboar lore tells how Agamaggan fell ten thousand years ago in the War of the Ancients. His blood raised giant thorn mazes across the plains, then sank beneath the soil and seeped into minerals. In time, it hardened into blood-red stones. The quilboar honor the shards as sacred remnants of their creator. They gather them from mineral seams and holy grounds, then use them as totems for battle and sorcery. Mangletooth is held in a cage at Camp Taurajo by the tauren. He bears a bitter grudge against his own kind, saying his tribe betrayed and cast him out. Without freedom or the magic of his people, he bargains with adventurers for blood shards. Their power lets him reach Agamaggan's magic despite his captivity and channel it to Horde champions. He takes pleasure in turning that power against the quilboar who rejected him. Mangletooth speaks with reverence of Razorfen, the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south. The tribes say the vast briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs grew from Agamaggan's colossal skeleton and tusks. They believe Razorfen Downs lies within the demigod's gaping maw, a holy threshold that devours and crushes any who enter without the Boar God's favor.

quest:506.text: Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir is free and carries news to Krusk in Tarren Mill. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, visited him and spoke of enslaving orcs who resist him. Perenolde also brought Elysa, a girl wearing the pendant the Warchief desires. Gol'dir has news for Krusk after a visit from Aliden Perenolde, head of the Syndicate. Perenolde called himself lord of the land and said he meant to enslave the orcs who resist him. His father and his mentor, the despised Blackmoore, had planned the same. Gol'dir sends you to carry this news to Krusk in Tarren Mill. He will follow after settling his own business where he is. Perenolde also brought his mistress, a slight girl named Elysa. Around her neck hung the pendant the Warchief desires.

quest:5062.text: Sacred Fire. Hunters seek Incendia Agave at the Boiling Pool to prepare a sacred fire that can call Arikara from the canyons of Thousand Needles. Motega Firemane instructs hunters to prepare the sacred fire of life, an ancient flame that calls the spirit beast Arikara. The monstrous wind serpent cannot simply be tracked across the canyon floor; she must be drawn to the fire. The flame needs more than ordinary kindling. Rare Incendia Agave, which grows around the scalding waters of Thousand Needles, feeds it. Incendia Agave grows near the Boiling Pool, below Darkcloud Pinnacle. To gather the spiky plants, you brave blistering waters and steam elementals drifting through the mists. Many bushels grow beneath the surface, where the hot lake water tests every hunter sent to collect them.

quest:5064.text: Grimtotem Spying. Cliffwatcher Longhorn tasks Horde champions with infiltrating Darkcloud Pinnacle to discover what the elusive Grimtotem clan is plotting. Three unknown couriers were spotted visiting the mesa, leaving guarded correspondence scattered across their mountaintop village. Uncovering these secret notes exposes a brewing scheme that threatens the tauren settlements of Thousand Needles. Freewind Post sits precariously on high spires, but its defenders must constantly look over their shoulders at their hostile cousins. The Grimtotem clan has long maintained a tense, resentful stance toward the Horde, clinging to their isolationist strongholds atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn noticed a shift in their behavior when three mysterious agents arrived over successive weeks, conferring with clan leadership in secret. Longhorn suspects these emissaries carried marching orders or alliances meant to undermine Thunder Bluff's presence in the canyon. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified network of sheer mesas connected by wooden rope bridges. Penetrating the village requires braving dense patrols of hostile Grimtotem warriors and shamans. Longhorn's scouts confirmed that the mysterious messages were locked away in separate chests spread across the outpost's central dwellings and outer bluffs. Securing the three secret notes requires sneaking or fighting across the entire settlement to snatch the clan's private communications from under their watchful eyes.

quest:5088.text: Arikara. Magatha Grimtotem sends a warning from Thunder Bluff: Arikara may be hunting High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. She sends Horde adventurers to summon and slay the ancient wind serpent on the burial spires of Thousand Needles. Magatha Grimtotem enchants the refined Incendia powder, a reagent, to call Arikara. She warns that ancient tauren traditions have changed too quickly under the new Horde alliance, stirring the vengeance of the ferocious wind serpent spirit. Magatha sends you south to the canyon of Thousand Needles. She tells you to cast the powder onto a ritual pyre among the elevated burial sites of Darkcloud Pinnacle.

quest:509.text: Elixir of Agony. In Hillsbrad Foothills, you gather toxic fungi from an overrun farmstead for Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. The Mudsnout Blossoms will fuel the Royal Apothecary Society’s experiments, as Lady Sylvanas seeks a plague against the living and the Scourge. The Scourge ravages the north, while the Alliance clings to towns like Southshore. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon works under the Dark Lady’s command to develop a plague against both. He finds alchemy tedious, yet gathers potent organic toxins from the countryside to brew elixirs meant to hasten the destruction of Sylvanas’s enemies. Nethander Stead lies south of Tarren Mill and east of the river. The abandoned human farmstead is overrun by vicious Mudsnout gnolls. Mudsnout Blossoms, foul-smelling mushrooms, grow among its filth and neglected soil. Their concentrated organic poisons are prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. You can cut through the gnoll packs or weave quietly past their ramshackle camps to gather them.

quest:513.text: Elixir of Agony. In the Undercity, Lydon's freshly mashed Mudsnout Composite awaits refinement. Apothecary Lydon sends it from Tarren Mill to Master Apothecary Faranell, who must treat it with a colloid of decay as the Royal Apothecary Society develops a new plague for the Forsaken. The Royal Apothecary Society sends raw discoveries from its regional researchers to the Undercity for specialized refinement. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon has mashed local Mudsnout Blossoms into a composite. Only the capital's laboratory holds the advanced reagents needed to bring his work to lethal fruition. Master Apothecary Faranell works under pressure in the Apothecarium. The Scourge threatens from the north, while aggressive human populations press from the south. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has demanded a potent new plague to defend the Forsaken. Lydon's composite could give Faranell the toxic breakthrough the Dark Lady expects.

quest:5147.text: Wanted - Arnak Grimtotem. Wanted: Arnak Grimtotem is a Horde bounty posted at Freewind Post demanding the execution of a violent Grimtotem exile. Arnak is targeted by the local authorities for murder and kidnapping on the mesas above the canyon. While tensions between the mainstream tauren of the Horde and the reclusive Grimtotem tribe are perpetually strained, Arnak took matters far beyond political friction. Branded an outcast, Arnak murdered a tauren and abducted the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong. In response to these heinous acts, Cliffwatcher Longhorn of Freewind Post sanctioned an open bounty calling for the rogue tauren's death. Arnak took refuge upon the high crags of Darkcloud Pinnacle, an extensive network of rope bridges and mesa encampments occupied by the Grimtotem clan near the entrance to Razorfen Downs. Trapped upon these windswept heights alongside Arnak is his captive, Lakota Windsong, awaiting rescue from anyone brave enough to fight across the Grimtotem bridges.

quest:515.text: Elixir of Agony. In the Undercity, Faranell prepares Lydon's mixture for a deadly purpose. The Royal Apothecary Society's new plague needs coastal reagents and alchemical draughts before the brew can be used. Apothecary Lydon sent his Mudsnout Blossom mixture from gnoll-held Nethander Stead to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell, head of the Royal Apothecary Society, saw its grim potential at once. Pleased by its toxic properties, he added his own colloid of decay. Then he named the catalysts needed to make the mixture a weapon. Lydon must gather precise reagents in Tarren Mill to activate the mixture's contaminating agents. Faranell calls for a restorative draught of Strong Troll's Blood to feed and steady the chemical reaction. He also needs organic parts from Hillsbrad's southern shore: scales from the serpentine Daggerspine naga and eyes from the coastal Torn Fin murlocs.

quest:5151.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Following a deadly centaur ambush on a merchant caravan in Thousand Needles, the goblin tinkerer Wizlo Bearingshiner was left as the sole survivor. Desperate to reclaim his prized invention, he hires adventurers to breach the wreckage, unlock an iron cage, and wrest the gizmo from the neck of a fearsome caged predator. Caravans venturing beneath the towering sandstone spires of Thousand Needles run a perilous gauntlet. Hostile centaur prowl the canyon floor, fiercely guarding their territory and raiding any travelers bold enough to pass through. When one such trade caravan was overrun just north of Whitereach Post, the centaur slaughtered the travelers and plundered the wagons, leaving only the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner to limp back to safety. In the chaos of the raid, the centaur looted nearly every valuable scrap, but they gave one ruined wagon a wide berth. Bound inside a sturdy transport cage was a ferocious, enraged panther with Wizlo's prized hypercapacitor gizmo fastened directly around its neck. Daunted by the predator's snarling fury, the centaur abandoned the cage intact, forcing Wizlo to entrust its key to brave mercenaries capable of slaying the beast and reclaiming his gadget.

quest:516.text: Beren's Peril. Scourge gather in a hidden cave in southern Silverpine Forest, and Shadow Priest Allister moves to stop them. The Forsaken hope to strike before the undead can begin their offensive. Shadow Priest Allister hears that servants of the Lich King are gathering deep in southern Silverpine Forest. Their growing numbers threaten Forsaken operations across the region. Allister sends scouts to strike first and destroy the Scourge in their secluded lair before they can mobilize. A hidden cave cuts into the hills south of Ambermill, the Dalaran-aligned settlement. The rough slopes make the cavern easy to miss, and the approach lies around the hills’ southern face. Ravenclaw drudgers and guardians dwell inside, remnants of the Scourge whose destruction helps the Forsaken hold their ground in the forest.

quest:517.text: Elixir of Agony. Apothecary Lydon’s work in Tarren Mill reaches a deadly test. His Elixir of Agony is ready, and he sends Horde champions to Dun Garok for a keg of Shindigger Stout. Apothecary Lydon serves the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas in Tarren Mill. He has gathered lethal ingredients from across Hillsbrad and finished a new concoction. Frogs and stray dogs are no test for its strength. Lydon wants to see what it does to living adversaries. Lydon needs a quiet way to carry his experiment. South of Hillsbrad, Ironforge dwarves hold the fortified stronghold of Dun Garok. He sends Horde agents into its underground barracks and mess halls to slip past dwarven rifles and axes and steal a keg of Shindigger Stout.

quest:518.text: The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara prepares to weaken Mug'Thol's ogres before striking at their hold in the Ruins of Alterac. She sends you after the Crushridge maulers. Mug'Thol and the Crushridge ogres hold the Ruins of Alterac. Melisara sees little chance of punishing Mug'Thol while so many ogres remain around him. First, their numbers must fall; only then can the next move begin. You are sent to hunt the Crushridge maulers.

quest:527.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken strike at the farms that feed the human town. High Executor Darthalia orders the attack from Tarren Mill under Varimathras's command. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign from Tarren Mill. Varimathras in the Undercity has ordered her to break the human resistance in Hillsbrad Foothills. Before attacking the defended town, Darthalia targets its northern fields. The farms feed the town, and disrupting them cuts provisions to the human militia while bringing disorder to the homesteads. The Forsaken press the human defenders while the Royal Apothecary Society works on a plague meant to destroy the living and the Scourge. Darthalia sees the fighting as a way to hold the humans down until the plague is ready. Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz are among the landowners killed in these early attacks.

quest:528.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, Forsaken forces press their assault south. After strikes on the northern farms, Horde operatives hunt the peasants fleeing to the orchards. The attack on Hillsbrad's human farms drives laborers south into the fields. After the northern farms are struck, many flee to the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad Fields, hoping to escape the advancing undead. High Executor Darthalia sees their flight as a chance to break the township's remaining labor force and morale. From Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia orders Horde forces to hunt the displaced laborers in the fields. The peasants have no protection, and their deaths choke Hillsbrad's food supply and weaken civilian resolve. For Darthalia and the Forsaken, each human killed tightens their hold over the surviving township and helps keep Lordaeron in Forsaken hands.

quest:529.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In the Hillsbrad Foothills, the Forsaken move against the humans resisting their advance. High Executor Darthalia orders the smithy in Hillsbrad Fields destroyed, hoping to cut off the weapons arming the local people. The Forsaken meet fiercer resistance in the Hillsbrad Foothills than High Executor Darthalia expected. Rural humans refuse to scatter or yield to the Deathstalkers and soldiers sent from Tarren Mill. The Forsaken learn that the peasantry are not fighting with pitchforks and scythes alone. In the fields, they are being armed for war. At the southwest edge of Hillsbrad Fields, Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices forge blades and armor for the militia from raw ore. Darthalia sends an operative to kill Verringtan, butcher his apprentices, and seize their stockpiled iron shipment. She aims to weaken the settlement's defense and use the metal in the eventual assault on Southshore.

quest:530.text: A Husband's Revenge. In the Undercity, Raleigh Andrean sends you after the friend who murdered his wife. An engraved ring from Silverpine Forest brings Raleigh Andrean's mortal memories back to him. He remembers his close friend Valdred Moray, who murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. The Scourge's chill and undeath have dulled Raleigh's grief and love, but his thirst for revenge remains. You are sent to find Valdred.

quest:532.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. Forsaken forces strike Hillsbrad town, aiming to break its human rule. High Executor Darthalia directs the assault from Tarren Mill. Hillsbrad's human defenders cling to their remaining authority despite heavy losses in the fields and patrols. High Executor Darthalia knows that peasants and militia rally behind the town's leaders. She sends Forsaken operatives into the Town Hall to kill Magistrate Burnside and five councilmen, cutting off the town's command. Darthalia aims to break Hillsbrad's civic life as well as its leadership. She orders operatives to burn the Hillsbrad Proclamation, a political document tied to the settlement's charter and pride. They also seize the town registry, taking official records and citizen rolls from surviving Alliance loyalists. The registry gives Undercity's intelligence a detailed view of the local people.

quest:5321.text: The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade struggles to stay awake on the road from Darkshore to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Newly awakened from a long sleep, he carries the Horn of Awakening and needs help against furbolgs and cultists along the way. Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw, has only recently awakened from sleep in the barrows. For millennia, the druids communed with wild spirits through the Emerald Dream. The Third War called them to wake, but centuries of hibernation leave Kerlonian struggling to stay conscious. He set out south from Darkshore to meet Liladris Moonriver in Ashenvale, yet exhaustion soon overtook him. Sudden naps leave him helpless along the wilds, so he depends on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep moving. The road from Darkshore into Ashenvale holds danger for Kerlonian. In Twilight Vale, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs stalk the roadway. Farther south in Ashenvale, members of the Dark Strand cult lie in ambush. Kerlonian may lie down wherever he stands when sleep takes him, so you need to keep watch and rouse him with the horn.

quest:533.text: Infiltration. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has at last heard word and rumor of Gol'dir. The Syndicate keeps moving the orc prisoner, and Krusk sends you to its large camp just north of town to bring back whatever information you can find. Krusk has at last heard word and rumor of Gol'dir, an orc prisoner held by the Syndicate. Its humans keep moving him, but the search has narrowed to their large camp just north of Tarren Mill. Krusk sends you there to find whatever information you can and carry it back. With each day, he fears Gol'dir's prospects grow darker.

quest:536.text: Down the Coast. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle leaves Southshore's defense to passing adventurers. Sent from Stormwind, he would rather drink ale than patrol, even as Torn Fin murlocs gather along the Western Strand. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle left Stormwind's city guard for a post in Southshore. The port feels dreary to him, and he cannot bear the fishy harbor odor. He spends his days drinking at the inn instead of patrolling the frontlines. Marshal Redpath has ordered him to protect Southshore from the dangers nearby, but Orinelle hires passing sellswords to do the work. The Western Strand runs along the coast west of Southshore. Orinelle scoffs at the murlocs as overgrown fish, but the Torn Fin tribe threatens coastal travel and local shipping. Its tidehunters and oracles gather in camps along the breakers and ambush anyone who strays too far from town walls. Clearing the shoreline means facing them there.

quest:5361.text: Family Tree. Cliffwatcher Longhorn asks you to carry a report to Nataka Longhorn, Cliffwatcher's brother, who is stationed in Desolace. Word of unusual centaur activity is meant to reach Ghost Walker Post. Nataka, Cliffwatcher's brother, holds a posting at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. A year has passed since Cliffwatcher last wrote, and in that time the centaurs have been behaving unusually. Nataka should hear of it, and you are asked to carry the report. The way runs to Stonetalon Mountain, which lies north of the Crossroads, then west into the Charred Vale. From there it turns south into Desolace, where a road runs south to Ghost Walker Post.

quest:5381.text: Hand of Iruxos. Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village says the Burning Blade holds a Demon Box, and that something powerful called the Hand of Iruxos is kept inside. At Mannoroc Coven, the Burning Blade makes use of it to open demon portals. Taiga sends you to Thunder Axe Fortress to fetch the box. Taiga Wisemane wants the flow of demons into our world stopped. You are given a demon pick, to be used on the red crystal inside Thunder Axe Fortress, which opens the way to the Demon Box. The box and the pick are to be brought back to Taiga in Shadowprey Village.

quest:5386.text: Catch of the Day. Cooked fish has not been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long time, and Nataka Longhorn would like that to change. Nataka rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers around, yet all the centaur activity leaves little time for the journey. You are asked to go in Nataka's place and bring back two Bloodbelly fish. No cooked fish has been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long while. Nataka Longhorn rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers, but with so much centaur activity there is little time to make the journey. So you are asked to go there, talk with the local fisherman Jinar'Zillen, and return with two Bloodbelly fish, Nataka's favorite. The road south of the post bends west and brings you to the troll village.

quest:539.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. Horde forces strike at Azurelode Mine in the Battle of Hillsbrad. High Executor Darthalia orders them to kill Foreman Bonds and his crew, cutting iron shipments to Alliance armories. High Executor Darthalia marked Azurelode Mine as vital to human strength after Horde forces seized the Hillsbrad Town Registry in earlier raids. The mine lies just south of Hillsbrad Fields, where workers keep extracting rich iron ore for Alliance weaponsmiths and armories. If the mine keeps operating, Southshore can rearm and strengthen its garrisons, undoing Tarren Mill's earlier victories. Darthalia orders Horde forces to kill Foreman Bonds, the human overseer, and a significant part of his workforce. The assault reaches into the mine's dark shafts to break production. It sends Southshore a clear warning: the Forsaken can reach its supply lines and isolated labor camps.

quest:54.text: Report to Goldshire. Report to Goldshire marks an adventurer's formal transition from the sheltered grounds of Northshire Valley into the broader jurisdiction of Elwynn Forest. Bearing dispatches from Marshal McBride to Marshal Dughan, recruits are granted Acting Deputy Status amid growing regional neglect from Stormwind's nobility. Having proven their mettle against local troubles within Northshire Valley, recruits are officially released from Northshire's local guard by Marshal McBride. In recognition of their service, McBride prepares transfer papers directing them south past the border gates along the road into Goldshire, transferring their responsibilities to the wider expanse of Elwynn Forest. Upon arrival in Goldshire, Marshal Dughan accepts McBride's dispatches and formally assigns the recruit the rank of Acting Deputy within the Stormwind Marshals. Yet Dughan's welcome comes with a grim warning: Northshire is a peaceful garden compared to the dangers roaming Elwynn, especially with Stormwind's royal army tied up in political maneuvering for distant nobles rather than protecting home ground.

quest:540.text: Preserving Knowledge. In Southshore, Loremaster Dibbs sends you to recover books from the Ruins of Alterac. Ogres have settled among the precious volumes left there, and one worn leather book matters most: it holds The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Loremaster Dibbs fears for the books in the Ruins of Alterac, where ogres have made their home. You are to search for the tomes they have looted and recover what you can. Dibbs would climb into the mountains to search as well, but fears old bones would not survive the journey. Among the tomes, Loremaster Dibbs most wants a worn leather book containing The Arm of Gri'lek. Dibbs is bent on learning the ancient troll lore inside, and the Ruins of Alterac were the last known home of an intact copy.

quest:541.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken turn their campaign on Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia sends Horde champions to break the dwarven garrison aiding local humans and kill its commander, Captain Ironhill. High Executor Darthalia has already pressed the human farmers and town militia across the foothills. Now she turns Tarren Mill's fury on Ironforge's troops. Dwarven soldiers have taken up arms for Southshore, strengthening the human presence in Lordaeron. Darthalia sees that alliance as an obstacle to be broken. She means to show the Alliance that helping the human survivors will bring devastation. Dun Garok is built against Thoradin's Wall in southeastern Hillsbrad. The fortified stronghold is held by disciplined mountaineers, skilled riflemen, and battle-hardened priests. To take it, Horde forces must break through those defenders and kill Captain Ironhill. His death breaks Ironforge's forward command in the region and leaves the remaining human enclaves isolated.

quest:5421.text: Fish in a Bucket. Jinar'Zillen of Shadowprey Village in Desolace likes to do as little as possible. Many shellfish traps sit below the village docks, and anyone who gathers the shellfish from them will be repaid with something worth having. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village, and would far rather someone else did the collecting. Anyone willing to take on that work is promised something they want in return: one fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

quest:544.text: Prison Break In. In Tarren Mill, Magus Wordeen Voidglare faces a crisis during his research. Months ago, four Forsaken fled the Undercity with artifacts stolen from a secure vault, and Sylvanas wants them back. Magus Wordeen Voidglare came to Tarren Mill to research, but now a crisis demands his attention. Four Forsaken turned from their brethren and stole from the Dark Lady. They broke into a secure vault and took four artifacts the apothecaries need for certain studies. Sylvanas wants them returned. The thieves fled the Undercity for Dalaran, where its wizards placed them in quarantine at the Lordamere Internment Camp. You are sent to find the traitors, recover the artifacts and report to Voidglare in Tarren Mill. There are four: a Bloodstone Wedge, Marble, Shard and Oval. Dermot holds the wedge, Ricter the marble, Alina the shard and Kegan Darkmar the oval.

quest:545.text: Dalaran Patrols. In Tarren Mill, Magus Wordeen Voidglare turns his attention to Dalaran's outskirts. Beyond the city's great dome, ruined streets may hold treasures of magical worth, but wizards and their elemental slaves patrol them. Voidglare wants the patrols thinned. After Prison Break In, Voidglare turns his attention to the wizards of Dalaran. They raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. Some say it protects them from the violence of the age; others say they sought solitude to study and plot. Voidglare cares nothing for their reason. Beyond the dome, the ruined outskirts may hold treasures of real magical worth, but wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. You are sent to hunt six Dalaran Summoners and twelve Elemental Slaves, then return to Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

quest:546.text: Souvenirs of Death. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa envies those sent against the human settlements of the Hillsbrad Foothills. He asks for thirty human skulls taken in battle for his collection. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign against Hillsbrad's human settlements. Deathguard Samsa remains on sentry duty in Tarren Mill, while others are sent to raid, burn, and pillage. He envies their chance to slaughter the living, a privilege denied to a guard fixed in place. Samsa hates the humans of Hillsbrad and collects the skulls of those slain in the campaign. He asks for thirty, not for an arcane rite or military plan, but as trophies from a war he longs to fight himself.

quest:547.text: Humbert's Sword. Near Dun Garok, Humbert's Sword is missing from its owner's camp. Deathguard Humbert had left to gather firewood while scouting the dwarven stronghold on High Executor Darthalia's orders. Ironforge scouts took his weapon, and he fears Darthalia will learn of his failure. Deathguard Humbert watches Dun Garok for High Executor Darthalia. He keeps a hidden post near the dwarven fortress. One morning, he leaves the camp briefly to gather firewood for boiling water. Ironforge scouts find the camp unguarded and loot it. When Humbert returns, his sword is gone, carried into the heavily defended bunker. Humbert knows losing his weapon to the enemy he was sent to watch could cost him his life under Forsaken command. If High Executor Darthalia learns what happened, he fears she will hang him from the rafters in Tarren Mill. He cannot storm Dun Garok alone, so he relies on passing Horde adventurers to recover his blade before his commander notices anything amiss.

quest:549.text: WANTED: Syndicate Personnel. On Tarren Mill's bounty board, Lady Sylvanas's decree condemns every Syndicate member to death. The Forsaken seek to clear the brigands from Durnholde Keep's ruins before they threaten Horde operations in the foothills. The Syndicate's sudden arrival southeast of Tarren Mill has drawn the Forsaken's attention. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her commanders see the Syndicate as an active pestilence, not displaced nobles to bargain with. The bounty orders immediate death. Any prisoners brought in will be executed without trial. Durnholde Keep, once an infamous internment fortress, now lies shattered and lawless. Syndicate Rogues and Watchmen have taken its crumbling ramparts and towers as an operations hub. High Executor Darthalia needs the armed bandits driven from the ruins to secure the road and protect Tarren Mill's southeastern approach.

quest:55.text: Morbent Fel. Above Raven Hill Cemetery, Morbent Fel's wards keep him beyond ordinary steel. Sven Yorgen sends you with Morbent's Bane to break those wards and end the necromancer's terror in western Duskwood. Morbent Fel haunts an abandoned house atop a rocky ridge just east of Sven's camp. The house looks over the sprawl of Raven Hill Cemetery. From there, the necromancer sends waves of undead through the surrounding forest and defiles Duskwood's graves. Dark magic and loyal undead thralls have kept ordinary steel from reaching him. Morbent Fel's wards turn a direct assault into suicide, deflecting conventional attacks. Sven entrusts you with Morbent's Bane, an enchanted artifact made to unravel that magical shielding. Invoke the relic and the barrier collapses, leaving Fel open to a mortal strike.

quest:550.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Hillsbrad, the Forsaken campaign has broken the human township's defenses. High Executor Darthalia sends you to carry her commendation to Varimathras in the Undercity. The fighting in Hillsbrad Foothills has been a brutal struggle for southern Lordaeron. From Tarren Mill, Horde champions struck at the township's farmers, militia, blacksmiths, and civic leaders. With Alliance forces crippled and the territory secured for the Forsaken, High Executor Darthalia prepares an official commendation so the champion's deeds reach the highest ranks of command. Darthalia's sealed commendation takes you to Varimathras in the Undercity's Royal Quarter. The dreadlord oversees military operations across Lordaeron beside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. The Scourge from the northern Plaguelands remains the Dark Lady's greatest threat, while surviving human enclaves still endanger the Forsaken's southern borders.

quest:5501.text: Bone Collector. At Kormek's Hut in Desolace, the goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle is certain that kodo bones are about to transform the world. Ten of them are wanted from the Kodo Graveyard, south of the hut, and something is promised in return. Bibbly insists the hut is sitting on a goldmine. Customers make furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder from kodo bones. Bibbly sends you south to the Kodo Graveyard to bring back ten of them, with something promised in return. A caravan comes by to pick up Bibbly's kodo bones, then sells them at Shadowprey Village. It is due any moment, and Bibbly is ten bones short of what is called a career high.

quest:552.text: Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand in Tarren Mill means to avenge Master Helcular, a great wizard on the brink of becoming a lich, who was killed by a human lynch mob after it found his ritual lair. Before vengeance can fall on Southshore, Thaivand needs Helcular's Rod, which one of the yeti there must hold. Master Helcular was on the brink of becoming a lich when he was found and killed by a human lynch mob, who had discovered the ritual lair he kept in the hills. They then buried the body in the Southshore cemetery. His apprentice, Thaivand, finds this disregard for a great wizard unacceptable and vows that the rains of vengeance will fall upon the town of Southshore. Thaivand says Helcular's Rod is needed first. Yeti have overtaken the ritual lair, and Thaivand is sure one of the beasts has the rod. There are so many yeti in the region that finding it will be difficult. Growless Cave and Darrow Hill are among the places they can be found.

quest:553.text: Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand hands you the Rod of Helcular. Three ceremonial pyres that Helcular fashioned for his most powerful spell must each charge it, and then it is to be driven into Helcular's grave in Southshore. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell, and the rod must be charged from each one. The flames of Azel and Veraz lie within the Foothill Caverns, in the yeti cave at Darrow Hill. The third, the Flame of Uzel, is found in a small cave above the caverns, farther north in the mountains, near Growless Cave. Once the rod is charged from all three flames, it is to be driven into Helcular's grave at Southshore, a heavily guarded human town. The graveyard sits in the northeast corner of the town, by the river, and the grave lies at the graveyard's southeastern corner.

quest:555.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. Southshore's Chef Jessen wants Soothing Turtle Bisque back on his tavern menu. Unrest has cut off his supply of snapjaw turtle meat, so he asks cooks to brave the northern waters near Dalaran and Lake Lordamere. Southshore is one of the Alliance's last intact coastal towns in Lordaeron, holding to civilian life amid growing strife. Chef Jessen says his cooking rivals any tavern north of Stormwind. Patrons supposedly travel from Darkshire in Duskwood to taste his Soothing Turtle Bisque. The rich soup depends on fresh meat from snapjaw turtles native to the rivers and lakes of the northern mountains. In calmer years, Jessen gathered turtle meat himself, traveling past Dalaran to Lordamere Lake's eastern shore. Rising tensions, hostile wildlife, the Syndicate, and Forsaken incursions have made the lands beyond town deadly for ordinary townsfolk. To keep the bisque on his menu, Jessen depends on armed travelers willing to gather meat from snapjaws along the riverbanks and northern shores.

quest:556.text: Stone Tokens. Stone Tokens is a Horde assignment issued by Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill to retrieve magical binding artifacts from Dalaran agents in the Alterac region. The Forsaken seek to study the arcane methods Dalaran's mages use to enslave and command powerful elementals. Gathering these inert tokens serves as the foundation for the Magus's research into elemental subjugation. The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized conduits and enchanted foci to bind creatures from other dimensions into servitude. While the city itself is still rebuilding, its agents and remnant forces patrol the surrounding territory, relying on elementals as laborers and defensive shock troops. Magus Voidglare, an arcane researcher working on behalf of the Forsaken in Tarren Mill, seeks to dissect the precise sorcery Dalaran uses to compel these entities into obedience.

quest:5561.text: Kodo Roundup. At Scrabblescrew's Camp in Desolace, Smeed Scrabblescrew is expecting a caravan and wants five tamed kodos ready for it. You carry Smeed's kodo kombobulator out among the ancient, aged and dying kodos, and lead the ones it tames back to the camp. Bibbly believes no other goblin in Desolace knows how to turn a profit. Smeed Scrabblescrew disagrees: the one caravan willing to brave this land depends on Smeed, and Smeed has formed a partnership with Cork and Rigger. The caravan is due at the camp shortly. Smeed built a device that can rejuvenate and bring under control aged and dying kodos. Aimed at an ancient, aged or dying kodo, it jolts the beast into a tamed kodo that follows you. You bring five of them back to Scrabblescrew's Camp, along with the device.

quest:557.text: Bracers of Binding. In Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil looks ahead to what the Magus may need next. The Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, and Bel'varil sends you to the ruins of Dalaran for four Bracers of Earth Binding. As the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Keeper Bel'varil expects another need to follow. Bracers of binding are worn on an elemental's wrists, where they bind the creature to a mage's service. Elementals wear them among the ruins of Dalaran. Bel'varil wants you to bring four Bracers of Earth Binding back to Tarren Mill.

quest:5581.text: Portals of the Legion. After Hand of Iruxos, Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village shows you the Hand and asks you to banish six demon portals at Mannoroc Coven, warning you to be wary of the portal guardians. Taiga Wisemane holds up the Hand of Iruxos, a grisly thing to look at, and says you must carry it if the demon portals around Mannoroc Coven are ever to be closed. The demon threat is increasing, and shutting the portals will check the number of demons crossing into this world. She wants all six portals banished, and she warns you to be wary of their guardians.

quest:559.text: Farren's Proof. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle sends Alliance recruits along Southshore's coast to prove his patrol's success. Marshal Redpath wants evidence that the murlocs have been cleared from the Western Strand. After the first coastal sweeps in Down the Coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle faces scrutiny from Marshal Redpath and Southshore's leaders. Farren claims the local murlocs have been cleared, but his superiors want proof. He leaves the grim work to wandering Alliance adventurers and sends them back to the shore for evidence of the kills. The Western Strand lies west of Southshore, where coastal murlocs live along the shallows. Farren asks for ten severed murloc heads to satisfy the garrison's officers. He detests the creatures and says their repulsive sight and smell have ruined his appetite for Southshore's chief export and staple food.

quest:56.text: The Night Watch. In Darkshire, Commander Althea Ebonlocke calls for help against the dead rising nearby. Stormwind’s garrison has left the town to its local militia, which depends on travelers to hold back the undead at Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Stormwind once protected Duskwood, but royal resources ran thin and political discord gripped the capital. The crown withdrew its commissioned soldiers, leaving Darkshire largely defenseless against the forest’s encroaching shadows. The people formed the Night Watch, a local militia led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke. It stands between the cursed forest and the town’s remaining residents. South of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery was once a peaceful resting place. Now it is an active burial site crawling with restless skeletons and reanimated spellcasters. The Night Watch is stretched thin along Duskwood’s borders, so Commander Ebonlocke directs arriving travelers to strike down Skeletal Warriors and Skeletal Mages before the dead spill onto the roads.

quest:560.text: Farren's Proof. At Southshore, Farren's Proof brings Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's report to Marshal Redpath. The murloc heads prove the work is done, though Farren will not carry them himself. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle patrols and secures Hillsbrad Foothills' southern coast, but the brutal work of frontier warfare turns his stomach. After you cull the murlocs along the beaches, he cannot bring himself to touch the severed heads you bring back as proof. He sends you across Southshore to deliver them to the town's command. Marshal Redpath oversees Southshore's defenses and military readiness as threats rise from Tarren Mill and wild beasts. He receives the sack of murloc heads from you instead of directly from Farren. Redpath knows you have become Farren's errand runner, but accepts the help. Southshore needs every willing hand to keep its borders safe.

quest:561.text: Farren's Proof. At Southshore, Farren's Proof carries Marshal Redpath's orders to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. The Marshal wants him to turn his attention to the naga pressing along the Eastern Strand. Marshal Redpath sends word across Southshore to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Fresh reports speak of naga incursions on the Eastern Strand, and the Marshal wants Orinelle to focus on that threat. He orders the lieutenant to set aside other concerns, drive back the naga, and report his progress in person.

quest:562.text: Stormwind Ho!. Alliance High Command fears the naga threat, and Stormwind Ho! gives Farren Orinelle a chance to leave Southshore. He hopes to take credit for their defeat and win a reassignment to Stormwind City. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle finds his Southshore posting miserable. The town sits on Lordaeron’s edge, hemmed in by Forsaken forces, syndicate brigands, and sea fiends. A city guardsman used to drunks and petty brawls in Stormwind, Farren longs to return south. His former mentor tells him Alliance High Command is increasingly anxious about naga encroaching on the coasts. Farren sees a chance to leave the north behind. Farren admits he lacks the courage and skill to face Daggerspine sirens and shorehunters in open combat. He commissions you to scour the beaches southeast of Southshore and cull the naga ranks. He needs your martial feats to write an impressive dispatch to Major Samuelson in Stormwind, and hopes the credit will help him secure a reassignment.

quest:563.text: Reassignment. In Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle seeks a way back to Stormwind. He has compiled an exaggerated report of his deeds against the coastal naga and sends an adventurer to Stormwind Keep to deliver it to his former mentor, Major Samuelson. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle resents his posting in the Hillsbrad Foothills. In Southshore, far from the capital and under Marshal Redpath's stern watch, he spends his days plotting a transfer south. He takes credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga to make himself look like an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ready for promotion. Farren wants a transfer without drawing Marshal Redpath's suspicion, so he goes around the local chain of command. He turns to Major Samuelson, a senior officer in Stormwind Keep who mentored him in the past. A report delivered straight to Samuelson puts Farren's claimed deeds before someone with authority over garrison assignments.

quest:564.text: Costly Menace. In Southshore, Darren Malvew fears the mountain lions coming down from Alterac. Undead, the Syndicate gang, and other scoundrels have cost the town horses, but Darren says the lions are the greatest threat. Darren Malvew of Southshore cannot bear losing the town's beautiful horses. Undead, the Syndicate gang, and scoundrels in the region have already cost the town quite a few. Darren says the greatest danger comes from mountain lions in Alterac, which keep descending from the hills. Darren wants eight Mountain Lions and ten Hulking Mountain Lions dealt with. Mountain Lions are found in the lower hills of the Alterac Mountains.

quest:5643.text: Shadowguard. In the Undercity, Aelthalyste sends a Darkspear priest back to Orgrimmar. She sees that the young troll is ready for the tribe’s sacred rites, and Ur'kyo awaits in the Valley of Spirits. Aelthalyste watches visiting troll priests in the Undercity. When an initiate has grown strong enough to face the tribe’s trials, she sends them across the Great Sea to learn from their own elders. She does not impose Forsaken teachings on them; their faith follows the traditions of their people. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo tends to the Darkspear tribe’s spiritual needs and ancient rites. He welcomes the returning initiate and prepares them for a rite of passage. It joins the priest’s bond to the loa with spells that ward off harm.

quest:5644.text: Devouring Plague. Across the sea, Devouring Plague awaits Forsaken priests who travel far from Lordaeron. Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff sends the adept to Aelthalyste in the Ruins of Lordaeron, where a signature form of Shadow magic awaits. In Thunder Bluff, Miles Welsh judges Forsaken priests who have honed their divine and shadowy disciplines. Posted among the tauren, he recognizes when an acolyte has grown strong enough for higher mysteries. Miles directs them back to the Ruins of Lordaeron rather than attempt to impart those teachings himself in Kalimdor. Beneath the city ruins, Aelthalyste waits in the Undercity's War Quarter. One of the foremost mentors of the Forsaken priesthood, she watches over acolytes who weave shadow. The Devouring Plague drains its victim and carries a corruptive force. Aelthalyste entrusts it only to those able to wield that force without succumbing to it.

quest:5645.text: A Lack of Fear. High Priest Rohan awaits in Ironforge to test the resilience of promising dwarven disciples. In the Mystic Ward, he offers teachings shaped for their growing strength of spirit. Priests serving the Alliance abroad are sent by local mentors to report to senior clergy of their order. Dwarven disciples answer that summons in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, where High Priest Rohan awaits. There, basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper uses of holy magic, tested through trials. Dwarven tradition teaches that the Light is both a shield and a strong defense in physical conflict. Reporting to High Priest Rohan shows that an initiate has endured the wider world's trials and has the mettle to master fear on the front lines.

quest:5646.text: Devouring Plague. In Orgrimmar, Devouring Plague training begins with Ur'kyo sending Forsaken priests home. They have come to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear, but Aelthalyste waits in Undercity to teach them the shadow arts of their own people. Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power in Orgrimmar. Among the Horde, Darkspear trolls and Forsaken share a curious bond in matters of faith, while orcs and tauren show little inclination toward priestly worship. Ur'kyo knows Forsaken initiates must master the shadow arts tied to their own condition. In respect between their peoples, he sends wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to complete their training. Beneath Lordaeron's ruins, Priestess Aelthalyste tends the flock in Undercity's War Quarter. Forsaken priests follow a solitary, grueling path shaped by their turn to shadow. They endure the painful touch of the Holy Light and learn to wield the devastating affliction of Shadow magic. When an initiate gains sufficient prowess, Aelthalyste gathers them close and teaches the affliction her kind calls Devouring Plague.

quest:567.text: Dangerous!. At Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia has marked four Hillsbrad humans for execution. She calls them enemies of the Forsaken for killing their people and striking at supplies. Across the Hillsbrad Foothills, the fighting is brutal and personal. High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill see ordinary Hillsbrad citizens as deadly foes. A wanted notice names four people whose resistance has killed Forsaken and cost them valuable shipments from the Undercity. The bounty names Clerk Horrace Whitesteed, who killed Deathguard Toma; Citizen Wilkes, who murdered Apothecary Eli; Miner Hackett, who killed Deathstalker Fry; and Farmer Kalaba, who sabotaged supply convoys from the Undercity. Each works from a different pocket of Hillsbrad resistance and remains elusive amid the wider conflict.

quest:5672.text: Elune's Grace. In Darnassus, young night elf priests answer a call from the Sisterhood of Elune. Their early journeys prepare them for deeper instruction from Priestess Alathea. The Sisterhood of Elune guides young acolytes in the Temple of the Moon, from their first prayers toward mastery of lunar magic. Night elves place their faith in the Mother Moon, Elune, unlike humans and dwarves, whose priests follow the Holy Light. When a novice priest reaches a milestone in devotion, senior mentors take notice and mark the disciple as ready to bear greater divine power. Priestess Alathea brings the Sisterhood's summons to the acolyte. She recognizes their dedication and welcomes them into traditions preserved across millennia. By accepting the rite, the priest seals a bond to Elune and gains access to protective wards and lunar invocations unique to the kaldorei faith.

quest:5674.text: Elune's Grace. From Dolanaar, night elf priests return to Darnassus for Elune's Grace. The rite marks their readiness to wield divine talents unique to their people. A priest's path in the Sisterhood of Elune calls for more than skill in prayers of mending and smiting. As acolytes gain experience, they reach a threshold where they may receive blessings granted only to the kaldorei. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar cannot bestow these deeper arts, so they send promising disciples to the spiritual heart of their order. Initiates cross Teldrassil to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Beneath the gaze of the high priesthood, Priestess Alathea judges whether each petitioner is ready to bear the goddess's defensive mantle. Elune's Grace is taught there as a divine talent reserved for the kaldorei.

quest:5676.text: Arcane Feedback. In Stormwind, Arcane Feedback prepares priests to face hostile spellcasters. High Priestess Laurena teaches the rite in the Cathedral of Light, where faith is shaped into a defense against arcane power. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena warns acolytes that arcane magic remains a danger. The Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order, while raw magic can turn volatile and lead to corruption or catastrophe. Warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts threaten the faithful. Priests learn that faith can become an active ward against spells around them. Arcane Feedback turns a hostile spellcaster's power back against them. The ward does more than deflect spells: it burns through the caster's mana and causes agony. Laurena teaches the rite to human priests preparing to travel beyond Stormwind, so the Cathedral's emissaries can face sorcery with a defense of their own.

quest:5677.text: Arcane Feedback. In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan directs human acolytes visiting Khaz Modan to seek their own teachings in Stormwind. The journey brings them to the Cathedral of Light, where human priests learn the traditions of their people. High Priest Rohan welcomes a human priest seeking deeper spiritual teaching in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward. Dwarven and human priests both serve the Holy Light, yet each people has its own rites, disciplines, and prayers of defense. Rohan keeps Ironforge’s teachings for his own clergy and sends human priests back to Elwynn, where they can learn the traditions of humankind. After reaching Stormwind City, the acolyte finds High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Laurena is relieved to see Rohan’s guidance reach the traveler, and welcomes them as their powers begin to grow. At the Cathedral, human priests can continue learning the spiritual practices of Stormwind and prepare to wield the Holy Light against the threats around the kingdom.

quest:5678.text: Arcane Feedback. In Darnassus, Arcane Feedback sends human priests back to Stormwind. Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon reluctantly honors the Alliance summons. There, High Priestess Laurena prepares the acolyte for deeper instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. She recognizes the formal alliance between the kaldorei and Stormwind, yet distrusts human magical and spiritual practices. Night elves see arcane power as volatile and dangerous, a view shaped by ten millennia of grief since the War of the Ancients. Even human divine rites trouble the night elf clergy when they blur radiant faith with arcane workings. Alathea honors the bond between the Alliance races and sends you to answer a recall from the Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena has sent couriers across the seas to gather human priests for advanced training. In Stormwind, you leave Elune's moonlit groves behind for the grand stone sanctuaries and golden radiance of the Holy Light.

quest:5679.text: Devouring Plague. Forsaken priests in the Undercity learn Devouring Plague from Priestess Aelthalyste. The rite is for those who have proven their dedication to shadow magic, and teaches a feared curse of the undead priesthood. In the Undercity’s War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste teaches Forsaken priests the grim arts of the Shadow. Priests of other races draw power from the Holy Light or ancestral spirits, but the Forsaken have shaped their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague gives form to that path: it torments foes and drains their stolen vitality to sustain the caster’s decaying body. Priestess Aelthalyste shares the plague’s power only with care. The spell is a weapon of potent malice, meant to turn the tide against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. As she teaches it, she warns her disciples to practice until their command is sure. Greater trials await those who seek mastery of the dark arts.

quest:568.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard the Horde's foothold in Stranglethorn Vale and protect their supply chain to Stonard. To keep that supply chain safe, he directs Horde champions to thin out the Lashtail Raptors outside Grom'gol Base Camp. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Commander Aggro'gosh carries the duty of protecting every member of the Horde within the jungle. The camp exists to keep supplies flowing safely to Stonard, but some of the local inhabitants are standing in the way. The raptors outside Grom'gol are the ones in the way. Aggro'gosh calls upon loyal fighters to thin out the Lashtail Raptors there, then report back to him for reassignment.

quest:569.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard Grom'gol's supply lines through Stranglethorn Vale. After the earlier hunt thinning the raptors outside the camp, a band of ogres encamped at the nearby Mizjah Ruins continues to harass supply caravans heading toward Stonard. The Horde's presence in northern Stranglethorn Vale is centered on supplying Stonard, an outpost of vital strategic interest. While Commander Aggro'gosh did not arrive with the intention of fighting every native group, a band of local Mosh'Ogg ogres has claimed the Mizjah Ruins southeast of the camp. Warnings have failed to stop their continuous raids against Horde supply shipments, prompting the commander to order a strike against the ogre brutes and witch doctors holding the ruins.

quest:57.text: The Night Watch. Darkshire's volunteer militia faces restless dead rising across Duskwood. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends travelers into the haunted barrows to hold the skeletal horrors back. The struggle helps keep Darkshire from falling to the darkness. Duskwood's graveyards have grown unnaturally restless as the forest sinks into twilight. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads Darkshire's volunteer militia, The Night Watch, against an endless siege. With no aid from Stormwind, her forces are stretched thin. Animated skeletons and other horrors rise from the earth and threaten the eastern settlements, so the militia calls on able travelers to enter the deadlands. Two places draw the militia's attention: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, just south of town, and Raven Hill Graveyard, far to the west. Skeletons pull themselves from forgotten tombs and shallow graves beside the roads, stirred by dark magic lingering in the forest's shadows. Cutting them down gives Darkshire's beleaguered citizens room to breathe, but the battle against this entrenched evil never ends.

quest:570.text: Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin seeks to harness the natural magic of Stranglethorn Vale for the benefit of the Horde. Building upon his previous rituals at Grom'gol Base Camp, he asks for sharp claws and a pristine feline fang to weave a powerful enchantment. Within Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin works to understand and bend the feral power of the wild to strengthen the Horde. Having seen success in his initial rites, he promises to craft a specialized enchanted relic for those willing to brave the dense underbrush and stalk the deadly predators prowling the surrounding territory. The ritual demands eight claws taken from shadowmaw panthers and a pristine fang from a tigress. Mok'thardin notes that while these fierce felines wander across Stranglethorn Vale, a gathering of them prowls south-eastward, just past the river running by the Mizjah Ruins.

quest:574.text: Special Forces. Following the reduction of the rogue colonel's rank-and-file soldiers, Sergeant Yohwa asks you to target the elite core of the compound. You are sent into the Stockpile cave to eliminate the commandos and headshrinkers before reporting to Lieutenant Doren. With the regular soldiers of the Kurzen Compound diminished through the work of the Second Rebellion, Sergeant Yohwa sets her sights on the colonel's elite specialists. She knows many of Kurzen's troops personally and calls them skilled, loyal and cruel. When they are not out in the wilderness slaughtering rebel soldiers, they are found in a cave at the back of the compound called the Stockpile. To break their strength, you are sent into the cavern to dispatch ten Kurzen Commandos and six Kurzen Headshrinkers. After the fight, Sergeant Yohwa tells you to report to her commanding officer, Lieutenant Doren, at the Rebel Camp, who will want your account firsthand.

quest:5741.text: Sceptre of Light. Azore Aldamort has heard that the Burning Blade of Thunder Axe Fortress, to the east, now hold the Sceptre of Light, which word says they obtained from the naga. Legend says it could sink whole cities beneath the great seas, and Azore will not let the Burning Blade keep such power. You are asked to bring it back to Ethel Rethor. Word has it that the naga's Sceptre of Light has come into the hands of the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress. Legend says it can sink whole cities beneath the great seas. Azore Aldamort holds that the Burning Blade cannot be allowed such power. A Burning Blade seer keeps the sceptre and studies it from the top of one of the fortress watchtowers. Azore wants you to take it from there yourself and carry it back to the tower at Ethel Rethor.

quest:5762.text: Hemet Nesingwary. This errand sends travelers across the sea from the salt pans of Kalimdor to the steaming jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Kravel Koalbeard, an opportunistic merchant at the Mirage Raceway, tasks adventurers with delivering a long-overdue package of specialty supplies to the renowned big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary. Out in the blinding expanse of the Shimmering Flats, commerce moves fast, but shipments sometimes lag behind. Kravel Koalbeard eventually receives a delayed crate earmarked for one of his wealthy patrons, Hemet Nesingwary. Having departed the Thousand Needles long before the parcel arrived, Hemet paid in advance to have it forwarded along to his wilderness hunting camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Rather than make the arduous trek himself, Kravel enlists roving adventurers willing to bridge the ocean divide. Tracking down Nesingwary's expedition north of Grom'gol Base Camp reveals the contents of the heavy crate: specialized heavy-gauge ammunition vital for bringing down the dangerous predators prowling the jungle. Hemet immediately recognizes the distinctive white crust of the salt flats clinging to the courier's gear, pleased that his old ties with the wily Kravel yielded the firepower his safari desperately needed.

quest:5763.text: Hunting in Stranglethorn. Roon Wildmane, a tauren in Desolace, once hunted beside a dwarf named Hemet. Now Roon sends you off with a kodo horn, bound for Hemet Nesingwary in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long ago a dwarf named Hemet came to Desolace, eager to hunt great beasts. Hemet handled a rifle with uncanny skill, and the two hunters passed many days together, the old enmity between their peoples set aside. When Hemet went off to Stranglethorn, Roon vowed to welcome Hemet back one day for another hunt, and Roon decides that time has arrived. You are to carry Roon's kodo horn to Hemet, who will know whose it is. Look in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp.

quest:578.text: The Stone of the Tides. Following rumours of a haunted isle off the jungle coast, Baron Revilgaz suspects an ancient troll relic has resurfaced. He directs explorers to scout the mysterious landmass and delivers a pass to research the artifact within the archives of Stormwind. Having learned of strange apparitions and water elementals haunting an offshore island in Stranglethorn Vale, Baron Revilgaz sees an opportunity. Suspecting that the goblin mage Gazban may have uncovered the fabled Stone of the Tides, the ruler of Booty Bay sends you to locate the island and confirm whether the rumors are true. To satisfy any curiosity about the relic, he provides a library scrip redeemable among the scholars in Stormwind.

quest:58.text: The Night Watch. In eastern Raven Hill, The Night Watch calls on outsiders to enter the crypts. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends them to destroy the plague spreaders while her guards defend Darkshire. This is the final mission in the town guard’s direct campaign against the undead overrun. Darkshire stands nearly alone, abandoned by Stormwind’s military and reliant on its civilian militia, The Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has spent her limited manpower guarding the crossroads, town perimeter, and supply lines. As the restless dead multiply across Duskwood, she turns to wandering champions to carry the fight into Raven Hill’s shadowed depths. The eastern mausoleum in Raven Hill Cemetery holds one of the region’s most dangerous concentrations of undead, unlike the open barrows. Its stone crypt teems with plague spreaders, ghouls whose afflictions can sicken the living. Destroying twenty gives The Night Watch room to breathe and helps keep Darkshire from facing a coordinated undead surge from the west.

quest:581.text: Hunt for Yenniku. Nimboya has returned from Orgrimmar to the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale to search for Yenniku, the youngest son of his chieftain. Suspecting the Bloodscalp tribe holds the youth captive, the scout asks you to hunt their warriors and take their tusks to demonstrate your strength. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nimboya speaks of a grim fate looming over Yenniku, the youngest son of the Darkspear chieftain. In accordance with an old tribal custom, the boy had been placed among the Gurubashi trolls of Zul'Gurub. When the Darkspear tribe departed their homeland alongside the orc warchief Thrall, Yenniku was left behind and lost. Sent back from distant Orgrimmar, Nimboya has undertaken the responsibility of finding the chieftain's son and bringing him to safety. Nimboya believes the Bloodscalp tribe now holds Yenniku. He demands proof that an adventurer is strong enough to hunt them. You are directed north to hunt Bloodscalp trolls and gather nine of their tusks. Bringing these trophies back to Grom'gol Base Camp proves your martial prowess and begins a longer pursuit to locate the chieftain's boy, leading directly into the hunt known as Headhunting.

quest:582.text: Headhunting. Nimboya at Grom'gol Base Camp needs to determine whether Yenniku, the son of the Darkspear chieftain, is dead. Adventurers are asked to hunt Bloodscalp headhunters and recover their shrunken heads so Nimboya can examine them. Following the search begun in Hunt for Yenniku, Nimboya worries that the chieftain's son may have already perished at the hands of the Bloodscalp tribe. To find out, he asks you to hunt the Bloodscalp Headhunters roaming the ruins of Zuuldaia and Zul'Kunda up the northern coast. By gathering twenty shrunken heads from them, Nimboya hopes to inspect the grisly trophies and confirm whether Yenniku met a violent end, cursing the Bloodscalp chief Gan'zulah if the youth was indeed slain.

quest:5821.text: Bodyguard for Hire. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally lead their kodo past the Kolkar centaur village, yet they stop whenever the centaur war drums are heard. Cork asks you to protect the caravan past the Kolkar village, and payment is waiting with Smeed Scrabblescrew, a bit down the road. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally take their kodo straight past the Kolkar centaur. Now and then the centaur war drums are heard, and the caravan stops, because dead traders make no profit. Cork asks you to guard the caravan past the Kolkar village, a short distance, and keep it in one piece. The caravan waits north of the Kolkar Village and southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress. Payment waits with Smeed Scrabblescrew at Scrabblescrew's Camp, a bit down the road. Smeed does a little business with the Gizelton caravan.

quest:583.text: Welcome to the Jungle. Barnil Stonepot welcomes newcomers arriving at the hunting camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Recognizing a fellow battle-tested wanderer, he arranges an introduction to the expedition's leader, the renowned huntsman Hemet Nesingwary. Barnil Stonepot greets newcomers at the camp in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, and he can tell a seasoned combatant when he sees one. He points out Hemet Nesingwary, a famous Alliance war hero and peerless tracker. Nesingwary reserves his fellowship for proven veterans, and Barnil believes the old marksman might be convinced to share his hunting wisdom with someone who has endured the trials of battle.

quest:5881.text: Calling in the Reserves. At Sun Rock Retreat, Calling in the Reserves sends you south to relieve a weary sentry at the Great Lift. Maggran Earthbinder gives you a letter for Grish Longrunner, who has stood watch far from home. Maggran Earthbinder keeps troop welfare and supplies in hand at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Across central Kalimdor, the Horde strains to keep its garrisons staffed, even in the years after the Third War. Maggran knows that endless watch duty wears seasoned soldiers down. He sends a reassignment letter south to the Great Lift, where Grish Longrunner has stood guard far from home. The Great Lift links the high southern Barrens to the canyons of Thousand Needles. When Grish receives Maggran's letter, he can leave his lonely watch over the lift mechanisms and return to his family. Fresh reserves can take his place.

quest:5943.text: Gizelton Caravan. Rigger Gizelton and Cork launched their caravan to get rich, and found the trade more dangerous than they expected. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead, and Rigger wants a capable adventurer to guard the caravan past it. Rigger Gizelton and Cork set up the caravan to make a fortune, and had no idea how risky turning a profit could be. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead. The demons usually leave the caravan alone, but this time the kodos are spooked. Rigger offers payment if you protect the caravan past the coven. Once it is safely through, your pay waits with Smeed, a business associate of theirs, at Scrabblescrew's Camp.

quest:596.text: Bloody Bone Necklaces. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp has his own agenda in Stranglethorn Vale beyond assisting Nimboya. He seeks to weaken the rival Bloodscalp tribe by gathering trophies from their warriors. Though Kin'weelay arrived in the jungle outpost of Grom'gol Base Camp to help Nimboya, he maintains private purposes of his own. The Bloodscalp trolls dwelling to the north are enemies of the Darkspears. Kin'weelay believes that claiming personal trophies from fallen foes bestows spiritual power over them, asking travelers to hunt Bloodscalp warriors and take the bloody bone necklaces they wear around their necks.

quest:601.text: Water Elementals. Following discoveries regarding the Stone of the Tides, Baron Revilgaz seeks a way to counteract the artifact's curse. He sends adventurers back to the island to harvest bracers from conjured water elementals so their magical residue can be inspected by experts. Believing the water elementals were summoned by the goblin wizard Gazban, Baron Revilgaz suspects their magical residue holds clues to dealing with the Stone of the Tides. The stone is said to curse anyone who wields it, causing the bearer to drift in and out of reality. To find a countermeasure, Revilgaz directs you back to the island off the coast to gather elemental bracers that might be scrutinized by the scholarly mages of Dalaran. Upon receiving the bracers, Revilgaz admits he lacks the specialized expertise to tell whether any of them will be of use. Rather than travel to Dalaran himself—he will not leave Booty Bay just to chat with tiresome old mages—he sends you north to have a mage look at them.

quest:602.text: Magical Analysis. Baron Revilgaz directs you northward from Booty Bay to consult the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Taking a bag of water elemental bracers, you seek out Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver to decipher the arcane curse tied to the Stone of the Tides. Following your hunt for the water elemental bracers, Baron Revilgaz hands over a bundle of their bracers. The goblin leader knows that unraveling the curse behind the Stone of the Tides requires deeper magical expertise than Booty Bay can provide. He directs you north toward the ruins of Dalaran, where the wizards remain deeply engaged in rebuilding their broken kingdom. Convinced that arcane scholars cannot ignore an intriguing puzzle, Revilgaz recommends seeking Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver directly, having had dealings with the knowledgeable wizard in the past.

quest:6027.text: Book of the Ancients. Azore Aldamort of the Ethel Rethor tower trusts you with a gem. Set in the hand of a serpent statue on Ranazjar Isle, northwest of the tower, it calls up the protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. After Sceptre of Light, Azore Aldamort hands you the Gem of the Serpent. A Serpent Statue stands on Ranazjar Isle, a little island to the northwest of the Ethel Rethor tower, and the gem belongs on its hand. That will bring forth the guardian of the Book of the Ancients, a book that holds naga secrets kept for centuries. Azore hopes it will teach much about their scaled foes.

quest:603.text: Ansirem's Key. Following his magical examination, Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver points toward an ancient troll dagger capable of disrupting the focal altar empowering the Stone of the Tides. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay. Ansirem Runeweaver determines that an altar or focal point amplifies the power of the Stone of the Tides. Overpowering that magic calls for another troll relic: an ancient dagger he found while researching in Stranglethorn. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay.

quest:605.text: Singing Blue Shards. Crank Fizzlebub seeks an enterprising adventurer to gather Singing Crystal Shards from the basilisks of Stranglethorn Vale. Competition with the Venture Company prevents him from harvesting the mineral deposits directly, leaving basilisk hides as the next best option. He promises a cut of the profits to anyone willing to bring him ten decent specimens. Crank Fizzlebub has identified an eager market for the Singing Crystals unique to Stranglethorn Vale. Unfortunately for his business ambitions, the aggressive presence of the Venture Company makes it hard for him to gather raw crystal in the field. To circumvent his rivals, Fizzlebub turns to an alternative method: basilisks consume the crystals, incorporating the mineral into their hardened hides, which allows usable shards to be retrieved from them instead. While any basilisk in the jungle might yield acceptable crystal fragments, Fizzlebub says the gentler ones are found along the shores south of Zul'Kunda, up north. Gathering ten shards allows him to move forward with his buyers, after which his business concerns shift toward the operations of the Venture Company itself.

quest:610.text: "Pretty Boy" Duncan. After tracking down Catelyn the Blade on behalf of her father, an adventurer learns that her weapon is no longer in her hands. She demands that her lost dagger be retrieved from a pirate named Pretty Boy Duncan before she cooperates further. Following the trail from Ansirem's Key leads directly to Catelyn the Blade, who ran away from a quiet life of scholarship and dusty tomes alongside mages. She cannot hand over her dagger at her father's request, since she no longer has it. If anyone hopes to secure her blade, they will first have to deal with the Bloodsail Buccaneer who took it. Catelyn suffered an uncharacteristic defeat at the hands of Pretty Boy Duncan, who struck her unconscious and made off with her signature weapon. As a fighter who relies on her personal knife, she insists on recovering that exact weapon from the buccaneer before anything else can move forward.

quest:6132.text: Get Me Out of Here!. Melizza Brimbuzzle traveled into the Valley of Spears hoping to do business with the Maraudines, but they would not talk, and she fears they mean to eat her. She asks you to get her out of there; her brother Hornizz will pay you handsomely. Melizza walked into the Valley of Spears to speak with the Maraudines, thinking she could strike a deal. They would not talk, and she suspects they would rather eat her. She says she overheard centaurs only minutes ago discussing wood for their cookpot, and she wants out quickly. Hornizz Brimbuzzle waits at the family camp, east of here and beside the kodo graveyard. Melizza promises that her brother will pay you well for bringing her out of the valley.

quest:6134.text: Ghost-o-plasm Round Up. Hornizz Brimbuzzle thinks there is money in the ghosts of the Valley of Bones. He figures the Magram centaurs would pay plenty for ghost energy, and he gives you a crate of ghost magnets to draw the spirits out. Hornizz points you southeast, to the Valley of Bones, where Magram ghosts walk. It sounds frightening, he admits, but surely it is scarier still for the Magram. He is sure that ghost energy captured there would be worth plenty to those centaurs. He hands you a crate of ghost magnets. Set down between the two huge skeletons in the valley, known as the Dead Goliaths, a magnet lures the ghosts toward it. From them you take ghost-o-plasm, which is what Hornizz plans to sell to the Magram. He wants eight ghost-o-plasms brought back to him, along with the crate.

quest:6141.text: Brother Anton. Brother Crowley speaks of Brother Anton, a fellow warrior who learned of undead in distant Kalimdor and booked passage at once to destroy them. Anton is looking for people with bravery and resolve, and waits in Nijel's Point in Desolace. Brother Crowley says rumors of an undead infestation in Desolace, a land in far-off Kalimdor, reached Anton, who immediately booked passage to seek and destroy the menace. Anton wants help from those with bravery and resolve. If your heart is true, Crowley tells you to speak with Anton in Nijel's Point, the Alliance town in Desolace.

quest:6142.text: Clam Bait. Mai'Lahii at Shadowprey Village has fished all his life and says the best bait is soft-shelled clam meat, which no fish can resist. He wants ten pieces, to be found around a wrecked ship up the coast to the north. Mai'Lahii has fished all his life, and he swears by soft-shelled clam meat as bait, since the fish cannot resist it. To the north, off the coast, lies a wrecked ship, and soft-shelled clams are scattered throughout that area. He asks for ten pieces of the meat.

quest:6143.text: Other Fish to Fry. Drulzegar Skraghook, a fisherman at Shadowprey Village in Desolace, lost the entire crew to the naga while fishing near Ranazjar Isle. Guilt weighs on Drulzegar, who asks you to go after the Slitherblade. Drulzegar Skraghook and the crew fished by Ranazjar Isle, which lies north of a wreck on the coast, and had done so many times. One morning the naga attacked and killed everyone except Drulzegar. Since then revenge is all Drulzegar thinks about, and the guilt is too much to bear. Drulzegar wants seven Slitherblade Myrmidons, seven Slitherblade Naga and five Slitherblade Sorceresses slain. A bad knee keeps Drulzegar from going along. The naga, Drulzegar says, usually lurk far down among the coral reefs beneath the waves, and the effort will be rewarded.

quest:616.text: The Haunted Isle. Krazek keeps his ears open for unusual rumors throughout Booty Bay on behalf of Baron Revilgaz. A tale shared by tavern sailors speaks of a haunted island off the coast, inhabited by water elementals and the ghost of a raving goblin. Delivering this rumor to Revilgaz piques the baron's interest in an ancient troll legend.
